hexcasting:get_caster.d: Adds me, the caster, to the stack.

hexcasting:entity_pos/eye.d: Transforms an entity on the stack into the position of its eyes. I should probably use this on myself.

hexcasting:entity_pos/foot.d: Transforms an entity on the stack into the position it is standing. I should probably use this on other entities.

hexcasting:get_entity_look.d: Transforms an entity on the stack into the direction it's looking in, as a unit vector.

hexcasting:get_entity_height.d: Transforms an entity on the stack into its height.

hexcasting:get_entity_velocity.d: Transforms an entity on the stack into the direction in which it's moving, with the speed of that movement as that direction's magnitude.

hexcasting:raycast.d: Combines two vectors (a position and a direction) into the answer to the question: If I stood at the position and looked in the direction, what block would I be looking at? Costs a negligible amount of media.

hexcasting:raycast/axis.d: Like [Archer's Distillation](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/basics@hexcasting:raycast), but instead returns a vector representing the answer to the question: Which *side* of the block am I looking at? Costs a negligible amount of media.

hexcasting:raycast/entity.d: Like [Archer's Distillation](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/basics@hexcasting:raycast), but instead returns the *entity* I am looking at. Costs a negligible amount of media.

hexcasting:get_media.d: Pushes the amount of media available to the current cast, in units of [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hexcasting:circle/impetus_pos.d: Returns the position of the [Impetus](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#greatwork/impetus) of this spell circle.

hexcasting:circle/impetus_dir.d: Returns the direction the [Impetus](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#greatwork/impetus) of this spell circle is facing as a unit vector.

hexcasting:circle/bounds/min.d: Returns the position of the lower-north-west corner of the bounds of this spell circle.

hexcasting:circle/bounds/max.d: Returns the position of the upper-south-east corner of the bounds of this spell circle.

hexcasting:swap.d: Swaps the top two iotas of the stack.

hexcasting:rotate.d: Yanks the iota third from the top of the stack to the top. [0, 1, 2] becomes [1, 2, 0].

hexcasting:rotate_reverse.d: Yanks the top iota to the third position. [0, 1, 2] becomes [2, 0, 1].

hexcasting:duplicate.d: Duplicates the top iota of the stack.

hexcasting:over.d: Copy the second-to-last iota of the stack to the top. [0, 1] becomes [0, 1, 0].

hexcasting:tuck.d: Copy the top iota of the stack, then put it under the second iota. [0, 1] becomes [1, 0, 1].

hexcasting:2dup.d: Copy the top two iotas of the stack. [0, 1] becomes [0, 1, 0, 1].

hexcasting:stack_len.d: Pushes the size of the stack as a number to the top of the stack. (For example, a stack of [0, 1] will become [0, 1, 2].)

hexcasting:duplicate_n.d: Removes the number at the top of the stack, then copies the top iota of the stack that number of times. (A count of 2 results in two of the iota on the stack, not three.)

hexcasting:fisherman.d: Grabs the element in the stack indexed by the number and brings it to the top. If the number is negative, instead moves the top element of the stack down that many elements.

hexcasting:fisherman/copy.d: Like [Fisherman's Gambit](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/stackmanip@hexcasting:fisherman), but instead of moving the iota, copies it.

hexcasting:swizzle.d: Rearranges the top elements of the stack based on the given numerical code, which is the index of the permutation wanted.

hexcasting:add.d: Remove the list at the top of the stack, then add all its elements to the end of the list at the top of the stack. | Perform addition. | Performs Addition, num will be treated as num + 0i. | Remove the Jump iota at the top of the stack, then add all its frames to the bottom of the Jump iota at the top of the stack. | Perform Addition | Adds two matrices together; they must have the same number of columns and rows. | Combines two motes into one, merging the mote records they point to. Any pointers to the second mote will become null, any pointers to the first will remain. This can make motes holding many more items than I could carry in a stack naturally! | Performs Addition | Remove the set at the top of the stack, then add all its elements to the set at the top of the stack. The two sets must be of matching type. | Removes the top two strings from the stack and combines them together. | Pushes a [text iota](https://miyucomics.github.io/hexpose/v/1.0.0/1.0.0/en_us#patterns/text_iotas) of the first followed immediately by the second.
hexcasting:add.i: list, list | num|vec, num|vec | complex, complex/num | jump, jump | long, long | mat, mat | mote, mote | qtrn, qtrn | set, set | str, str | text, text
hexcasting:add.o: list | num|vec | complex | jump | long | mat | mote | quaternion | set | str | text

hexcasting:sub.d: Perform subtraction. | Performs Subtraction, num will be treated as num + 0i. | Perform Subtraction | Performs Subtraction | Remove the set at the top of the stack, then remove all its elements from the set at the top of the stack. The two sets must be of matching type.
hexcasting:sub.i: num|vec, num|vec | complex, complex/num | long, long | qrtn, qtrn | set, set

hexcasting:mul.d: Perform multiplication or the dot product. | Calculates the outer product of two lists. The resulting list has an entry for every possible pairing between the input lists. | Performs Multiplication | Pushes a list containing every combination of elements between the two lists. | Perform Multiplication | Multiplies the first n by m by with an m by p matrix to get an n by p matrix. | Performs Multiplication, Scalar if a num & quat are given, Hamiltonian if 2 quaternions are given.
hexcasting:mul.i: num|vec, num|vec | [a], [b] | complex, num | list, list | long, long | mat, mat | quaternion, num
hexcasting:mul.o: num|vec | [[a, b]] | complex | list | long | mat | quaternion

hexcasting:div.d: Perform division or the cross product. | Calculates the inner product of two lists. If the two lists were arranged side-by-side, the resulting list has one entry for every row (unpaired elements are skipped). | Performs Scalar Division. | Pushes a list containing pairs of values corresponding to the values at that index in each list. | Perform Floored Division | Divides the first n by m matrix with an m by m matrix to get an n by m matrix. | Performs Scalar Division.
hexcasting:div.i: num|vec, num|vec | [a], [b] | complex, num | list, list | long, long | mat, mat | quaternion, num
hexcasting:div.o: num|vec | [[a, b]] | complex | list | long | mat | quaternion

hexcasting:abs.d: Convert a boolean to a number; True becomes 1, and False becomes 0. | Remove the list at the top of the stack, then push the number of elements in the list to the stack. | Compute the absolute value or length. | Pushes the Argument (the length). | Pushes the number of entries in the Dictionary | Consumes a gate iota, returns how many entities are marked by that gate. | Transforms the Item Stack at the top of the stack into its size. | Remove the Jump iota at the top of the stack, then push the number of frames within it to the stack. | Accepts a mote and returns the number of items in the record referenced by that mote. | Pushes the Argument (the length). | Remove the set at the top of the stack, then push the number of elements in the set to the stack. | Removes a string and returns its length. | Pushes the length of the [text iota](https://miyucomics.github.io/hexpose/v/1.0.0/1.0.0/en_us#patterns/text_iotas).
hexcasting:abs.i: bool | list | num|vec | complex | dict | gate | item stack | jump | mote | quaternion | set | str | text
hexcasting:abs.o: number | num | number | num | num | num | int | num | int | num | num | num | number

hexcasting:pow.d: Perform exponentiation or vector projection. | Accepts a square matrix and an integer, and raises the matrix to the power of the integer. | Performs Exponentiation.
hexcasting:pow.i: num|vec, num|vec | mat, int | num, complex

hexcasting:floor.d: "Floors" a number, cutting off the fractional component and leaving an integer value. If passed a vector, instead floors each of its components.

hexcasting:ceil.d: "Ceilings" a number, raising it to the next integer value if it has a fractional component. If passed a vector, instead ceils each of its components.

hexcasting:construct_vec.d: Combine three numbers at the top of the stack into a vector's X, Y, and Z components (bottom to top).

hexcasting:deconstruct_vec.d: Split a vector into its X, Y, and Z components (bottom to top).

hexcasting:coerce_axial.d: For a vector, coerce it to its nearest axial direction, a unit vector. For a number, return the sign of the number; 1 if positive, -1 if negative. In both cases, zero is unaffected.

hexcasting:and.d: Takes the intersection of two sets. | Returns True if both arguments are true; otherwise returns False. | Perform Bitwise AND | Takes the intersection of two sets. The new set will only contain elements that were present in both of the previous sets. The two sets must be of matching type.
hexcasting:and.i: (num, num)|(list, list) | bool, bool | long, long | set, set

hexcasting:or.d: Unifies two sets. | Returns True if at least one of the arguments are True; otherwise returns False. | Perform Bitwise OR
hexcasting:or.i: (num, num)|(list, list) | bool, bool | long, long

hexcasting:not.d: If the argument is True, return False; if it is False, return True. | Takes the inversion of a bitset, changing all "on" bits to "off" and vice versa. In my experience, this will take the form of that number negated and decreased by one. For example, 0 will become -1, and -100 will become 99. | Perform Bitwise NOT

hexcasting:xor.d: Takes the exclusive disjunction of two sets. | Returns True if exactly one of the arguments is true; otherwise returns False. | Perform Bitwise XOR | Takes the exclusive disjunction of two sets. The new set will only contain elements that were present in only one of the two sets. The two sets must be of matching type.
hexcasting:xor.i: (num, num)|(list, list) | bool, bool | long, long | set, set

hexcasting:greater.d: If the first argument is greater than the second, return True. Otherwise, return False. | If the first vector is longer than the second, return True. Otherwise, return False.

hexcasting:less.d: If the first argument is less than the second, return True. Otherwise, return False. | If the first vector is shorter than the second, return True. Otherwise, return False.

hexcasting:greater_eq.d: If the first argument is greater than or equal to the second, return True. Otherwise, return False. | If the first vector is longer or the same length as the second, return True. Otherwise, return False.

hexcasting:less_eq.d: If the first argument is less than or equal to the second, return True. Otherwise, return False. | If the first vector is shorter or the same length as the second, return True. Otherwise, return False.

hexcasting:equals.d: If the first argument equals the second (within a small tolerance), return True. Otherwise, return False.

hexcasting:not_equals.d: If the first argument does not equal the second (outside a small tolerance), return True. Otherwise, return False.

hexcasting:type_equals.d: Compare the given iotas and push whether they are of the same type.

hexcasting:type_not_equals.d: Compare the given iotas and push whether they are of different types.

hexcasting:bool_coerce.d: Convert an argument to a boolean. The number 0, Null, False, the vector (0, 0, 0), and the empty list become False; everything else becomes True.

hexcasting:if.d: If the first argument is True, keeps the second and discards the third; otherwise discards the second and keeps the third.

hexcasting:random.d: Creates a random number between 0 and 1.

hexcasting:sin.d: Takes the sine of an angle in radians, yielding the vertical component of that angle drawn on a unit circle. Related to the values of [π](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/consts@hexcasting:const/double/pi) and [τ](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/consts@hexcasting:const/double/tau).

hexcasting:cos.d: Takes the cosine of an angle in radians, yielding the horizontal component of that angle drawn on a unit circle. Related to the values of [π](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/consts@hexcasting:const/double/pi) and [τ](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/consts@hexcasting:const/double/tau).

hexcasting:tan.d: Takes the tangent of an angle in radians, yielding the slope of that angle drawn on a circle. Related to the values of [π](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/consts@hexcasting:const/double/pi) and [τ](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/consts@hexcasting:const/double/tau).

hexcasting:arcsin.d: Takes the inverse sine of a value with absolute value 1 or less, yielding the angle whose sine is that value. Related to the values of [π](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/consts@hexcasting:const/double/pi) and [τ](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/consts@hexcasting:const/double/tau).

hexcasting:arccos.d: Takes the inverse cosine of a value with absolute value 1 or less, yielding the angle whose cosine is that value. Related to the values of [π](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/consts@hexcasting:const/double/pi) and [τ](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/consts@hexcasting:const/double/tau).

hexcasting:arctan.d: Takes the inverse tangent of a value, yielding the angle whose tangent is that value. Related to the values of [π](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/consts@hexcasting:const/double/pi) and [τ](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/consts@hexcasting:const/double/tau).

hexcasting:arctan2.d: Takes the inverse tangent of a Y and X value, yielding the angle between the X-axis and a line from the origin to that point.

hexcasting:logarithm.d: Removes the number at the top of the stack, then takes the logarithm of the number at the top using the other number as its base. Related to the value of [*e*](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/consts@hexcasting:const/double/e).

hexcasting:modulo.d: Takes the modulus of two numbers. This is the amount *remaining* after division - for example, 5 % 2 is 1, and 5 % 3 is 2. When applied on vectors, performs the above operation elementwise.

hexcasting:unique.d: Removes duplicate entries from a list. | Keeps only the first instance of any glyph in the text. Styling is enough to distinguish a glyph.

hexcasting:print.d: Displays the top iota of the stack to me.

hexcasting:explode.d: Remove a number and vector from the stack, then create an explosion at the given location with the given power.

hexcasting:explode/fire.d: Remove a number and vector from the stack, then create a fiery explosion at the given location with the given power.

hexcasting:add_motion.d:
Remove an entity and direction from the stack, then give a shove to the given entity in the given direction. The strength of the impulse is determined by the length of the vector.
Costs units of [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst) equal to the square of the length of the vector, plus one for every Impulse except the first targeting an entity.

hexcasting:blink.d:
Remove an entity and length from the stack, then teleport the given entity along its look vector by the given length.
Costs about one [Amethyst Shard](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst) per two blocks travelled.

hexcasting:break_block.d:
Remove a location from the stack, then break the block at the given location. This spell can break nearly anything a Diamond Pickaxe can break.
Costs about an eighth of one [Amethyst Dust, or a negligible amount if breaking a ](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst)[](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/spells/blockworks@hexcasting:conjure_block)[Conjured Block](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/spells/blockworks@hexcasting:conjure_block) or [Conjured Light](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/spells/blockworks@hexcasting:conjure_light).

hexcasting:place_block.d:
Remove a location from the stack, then pick a block item and place it at the given location.
Costs about an eighth of one [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hexcasting:colorize.d: I must be holding a [Pigment](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/pigments) in my other hand to cast this spell. When I do, it will consume the dye and permanently change my mind's coloration (at least, until I cast the spell again). Costs about one [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hexcasting:cycle_variant.d: Certain items I create seem oddly receptive to the influence of media. By holding a [Cypher](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/hexcasting), [Trinket](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/hexcasting), [Artifact](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/hexcasting), [Focus](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/focus), or [Spellbook](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/spellbook) in my other hand, I can use this spell to change the appearance of the item. Costs a negligible amount of media.

hexcasting:create_water.d: Summon a block of water (or insert up to a bucket's worth) into a block at the given position. Costs about one [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hexcasting:destroy_water.d: Drains either a liquid container at, or a body of liquid around, the given position. Costs about two [Charged Amethyst](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hexcasting:ignite.d: Start a fire on top of the given location, as if a Fire Charge was applied, or set fire to an entity. Costs about one [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hexcasting:extinguish.d: Extinguish blocks in a large area. Costs about six [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hexcasting:conjure_block.d: Conjure an ethereal, but solid, block that sparkles with my pigment at the given position. Costs about one [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hexcasting:conjure_light.d: Conjure a magical light that softly glows with my pigment at the given position. Costs about one [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hexcasting:bonemeal.d: Encourage a plant or sapling at the target position to grow, as if Bonemeal was applied. Costs a bit more than one [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hexcasting:recharge.d: Recharge a media-containing item in my other hand. Costs about one [Amethyst Shard](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst) per item.

hexcasting:erase.d: Clears Hex-containing or iota-containing items in my other hand. Costs about one [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst) per item.

hexcasting:edify.d: Forcibly infuse media into the sapling at the target position, causing it to grow into an [Edified Tree](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/edified). Costs about one [Charged Amethyst](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hexcasting:beep.d: Remove a vector and two numbers from the stack. Plays an instrument defined by the first number at the given location, with a note defined by the second number. Costs a negligible amount of media.

hexcasting:potion/weakness.d: Inflicts weakness. Base cost is one [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst) per 10 seconds.

hexcasting:potion/levitation.d: Inflicts levitation. Base cost is one [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst) per 5 seconds.

hexcasting:potion/wither.d: Inflicts withering. Base cost is one [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst) per second.

hexcasting:potion/poison.d: Inflicts poison. Base cost is one [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst) per 3 seconds.

hexcasting:potion/slowness.d: Inflicts slowness. Base cost is one [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst) per 5 seconds.

hexcasting:flight/range.d: A flight limited in its range.

hexcasting:flight/time.d: A flight limited in its duration.

hexcasting:flight/can_fly.d: Returns whether the given player is under the effects of [Anchorite's](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/spells/flight@hexcasting:flight/range) or [Wayfarer's Flight](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/spells/flight@hexcasting:flight/time).

hexcasting:sentinel/create.d: Summons my [sentinel](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/spells/sentinels) at the given position. Costs about one [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hexcasting:sentinel/destroy.d: Banish my [sentinel](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/spells/sentinels), and remove it from the world. Costs a negligible amount of media.

hexcasting:sentinel/get_pos.d: Add the position of my [sentinel](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/spells/sentinels) to the stack, or Null if it isn't summoned. Costs a negligible amount of media.

hexcasting:sentinel/wayfind.d: Transform the position vector on the top of the stack into a unit vector pointing from that position to my [sentinel](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/spells/sentinels), or Null if it isn't summoned. Costs a negligible amount of media.

hexcasting:akashic/read.d: Read the iota associated with the given pattern out of the [Akashic Library](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#greatwork/akashiclib) with its [Record](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#greatwork/akashiclib) at the given position. This has no range limit. Costs about one [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hexcasting:akashic/write.d: Associate the iota with the given pattern in the [Akashic Library](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#greatwork/akashiclib) with its [Record](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#greatwork/akashiclib) at the given position. This *does* have a range limit. Costs about one [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hexcasting:escape.d: Similar to [Contemplation](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/patterns_as_iotas@hexcasting:runtime_escape), but acts even when drawn between [Intro-](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/patterns_as_iotas@hexcasting:open_paren) and [Retrospection](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/patterns_as_iotas@hexcasting:close_paren). This can "escape" other patterns that work between [Intro-](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/patterns_as_iotas@hexcasting:open_paren) and [Retrospection](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/patterns_as_iotas@hexcasting:close_paren), putting them into the list without any other effects.

hexcasting:runtime_escape.d: To use [Contemplation](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/patterns_as_iotas@hexcasting:runtime_escape), I draw it, then another arbitrary pattern. That second pattern is added to the stack.

hexcasting:open_paren.d: Drawing [Introspection](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/patterns_as_iotas@hexcasting:open_paren) makes my drawing of patterns act differently, for a time. Until I draw [Retrospection](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/patterns_as_iotas@hexcasting:close_paren), the patterns I draw are saved. Then, when I draw [Retrospection](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/patterns_as_iotas@hexcasting:close_paren), they are added to the stack as a list iota.

hexcasting:close_paren.d: If I draw another [Introspection](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/patterns_as_iotas@hexcasting:close_paren), it'll still be saved to the list, but I'll then have to draw *two* [Retrospections](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/patterns_as_iotas@hexcasting:close_paren) to get back to normal casting.

hexcasting:open_n_parens.d: Removes a number from the stack, then acts as though I'd drawn that many [Introspections](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/patterns_as_iotas@hexcasting:open_paren). Treated as a normal pattern while [introspecting](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/patterns_as_iotas@hexcasting:open_paren), so nesting this may require [tricks](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/patterns_as_iotas@hexcasting:escape) to draw extra [Retrospections](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/patterns_as_iotas@hexcasting:close_paren).

hexcasting:close_all_parens.d: Works like [Retrospection](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/patterns_as_iotas@hexcasting:close_paren), but closes *all* open [Introspections](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/patterns_as_iotas@hexcasting:open_paren) at once. The number of layers closed, along with the list of saved patterns, are then added to the stack.

hexcasting:read_into_parens.d: Only works while [introspecting](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/patterns_as_iotas@hexcasting:open_paren). Reads an iota from my offhand, and adds it to the in-progress list. For iotas other than patterns, I may need to [take steps](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/patterns_as_iotas@iota_embedding) to avoid a mishap when executing the list.

hexcasting:undo.d: Finally, if I make a mistake while drawing patterns inside [Intro-](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/patterns_as_iotas@hexcasting:open_paren) and [Retrospection](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/patterns_as_iotas@hexcasting:close_paren), I can draw [Evanition](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/patterns_as_iotas@hexcasting:undo) to remove the last pattern that I drew from the pattern list that is being constructed.

hexcasting:eval.d: Remove something evaluatable (usually a pattern or an [entire Hex](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#casting/whats_a_hex)) from the stack, then cast it as if I had drawn the relevant patterns with my [Staff](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/staff).

hexcasting:eval/cc.d: Cast something evaluatable from the stack exactly like [Hermes' Gambit](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/meta@hexcasting:eval), except that a unique "Jump" iota is pushed to the stack beforehand.

hexcasting:halt.d: This pattern forcibly halts a Hex. This is mostly useless on its own, as I could simply just stop writing patterns, or put down my staff.

hexcasting:read.d: Copy the iota stored in the item in my other hand and add it to the stack.

hexcasting:read/entity.d: Like [Scribe's Reflection](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/readwrite@hexcasting:read), but the iota is read out of an entity instead of my other hand. | Like [Scribe's Reflection](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/readwrite@hexcasting:read), but the iota is read out of a block instead of my other hand.

hexcasting:write.d: Remove the top iota from the stack, and save it into the item in my other hand.

hexcasting:write/entity.d:
Like [Scribe's Gambit](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/readwrite@hexcasting:read), but the iota is written to an entity instead of my other hand.
Interestingly enough, it looks like I cannot write my own Name using this spell. I get a sense that I might be endangered if I could. | Like [Scribe's Gambit](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/readwrite@hexcasting:write), but the iota is written to a block instead of my other hand.
Interestingly enough, it looks like I cannot write my own Name using this spell. I get a sense that I might be endangered if I could.

hexcasting:readable.d: If the item in my other hand holds an iota I can read, returns True. Otherwise, returns False.

hexcasting:readable/entity.d: Like [Auditor's Reflection](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/readwrite@hexcasting:readable), but the readability of an entity is checked instead of my other hand. | Like [Auditor's Reflection](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/readwrite@hexcasting:readable), but the readability of a block is checked instead of my other hand.

hexcasting:writable.d: If I could save an iota into the item in my other hand, returns True. Otherwise, returns False.

hexcasting:writable/entity.d: Like [Assessor's Reflection](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/readwrite@hexcasting:writable), but the writability of an entity is checked instead of my other hand. | Like [Assessor's Reflection](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/readwrite@hexcasting:writable), but the writability of a block is checked instead of my other hand.

hexcasting:read/local.d: Copy the iota out of my [ravenmind](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/readwrite@hexcasting:local), which I likely just wrote with [Huginn's Gambit](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/readwrite@hexcasting:write/local).

hexcasting:write/local.d: Removes the top iota from the stack, and saves it to my [ravenmind](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/readwrite@hexcasting:local), storing it there until I stop casting the Hex.

hexcasting:thanatos.d: It seems there is a limit to how many patterns can be evaluated within a single Hex. I can use this pattern to deterime how many patterns remain before I reach this limit.

hexcasting:const/null.d: Adds the Null influence to the top of the stack.

hexcasting:const/true.d: Adds True to the top of the stack.

hexcasting:const/false.d: Adds False to the top of the stack.

hexcasting:const/vec/px.d: The left-hand counter-clockwise pattern adds (1, 0, 0) to the stack; the right-hand clockwise pattern adds (-1, 0, 0).

hexcasting:const/vec/py.d: The left-hand counter-clockwise pattern adds (0, 1, 0) to the stack; the right-hand clockwise pattern adds (0, -1, 0).

hexcasting:const/vec/pz.d: The left-hand counter-clockwise pattern adds (0, 0, 1); the right-hand clockwise pattern adds (0, 0, -1).

hexcasting:const/vec/nx.d: The left-hand counter-clockwise pattern adds (1, 0, 0) to the stack; the right-hand clockwise pattern adds (-1, 0, 0).

hexcasting:const/vec/ny.d: The left-hand counter-clockwise pattern adds (0, 1, 0) to the stack; the right-hand clockwise pattern adds (0, -1, 0).

hexcasting:const/vec/nz.d: The left-hand counter-clockwise pattern adds (0, 0, 1); the right-hand clockwise pattern adds (0, 0, -1).

hexcasting:const/double/pi.d: Adds π, the radial representation of half a circle, to the stack.

hexcasting:const/double/tau.d: Adds τ, the radial representation of a complete circle, to the stack.

hexcasting:const/double/e.d: Adds *e*, the base of natural logarithms, to the stack.

hexcasting:const/double/phi.d: Adds φ, the golden ratio, to the stack. This is the ratio between two values such that (A+B)/A = A/B.

hexcasting:get_entity.d: Transform the position on the stack into the entity at that location (or Null if there isn't one).

hexcasting:get_entity/animal.d: Transform the position on the stack into the animal at that location (or Null if there isn't one).

hexcasting:get_entity/monster.d: Transform the position on the stack into the monster at that location (or Null if there isn't one).

hexcasting:get_entity/item.d: Transform the position on the stack into the dropped item at that location (or Null if there isn't one).

hexcasting:get_entity/player.d: Transform the position on the stack into the player at that location (or Null if there isn't one).

hexcasting:get_entity/living.d: Transform the position on the stack into the living creature at that location (or Null if there isn't one).

hexcasting:zone_entity.d: Take a position and maximum distance on the stack, and combine them into a list of all entities near the position.

hexcasting:zone_entity/animal.d: Take a position and maximum distance on the stack, and combine them into a list of animals near the position.

hexcasting:zone_entity/not_animal.d: Take a position and maximum distance on the stack, and combine them into a list of non-animal entities near the position.

hexcasting:zone_entity/monster.d: Take a position and maximum distance on the stack, and combine them into a list of monsters near the position.

hexcasting:zone_entity/not_monster.d: Take a position and maximum distance on the stack, and combine them into a list of non-monster entities near the position.

hexcasting:zone_entity/item.d: Take a position and maximum distance on the stack, and combine them into a list of dropped items near the position.

hexcasting:zone_entity/not_item.d: Take a position and maximum distance on the stack, and combine them into a list of non-dropped-item entities near the position.

hexcasting:zone_entity/player.d: Take a position and maximum distance on the stack, and combine them into a list of players near the position.

hexcasting:zone_entity/not_player.d: Take a position and maximum distance on the stack, and combine them into a list of non-player characters near the position.

hexcasting:zone_entity/living.d: Take a position and maximum distance on the stack, and combine them into a list of living creatures near the position.

hexcasting:zone_entity/not_living.d: Take a position and maximum distance on the stack, and combine them into a list of non-living entities near the position.

hexcasting:compare_block/lenient.d: Compare the blocks specified by the given vectors and push whether they are of the same type. Two [Edified Stairs](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/edified@hexcasting:cut_edified_plank_variants) will always compare as equal regardless of their shape or if they are waterlogged.

hexcasting:compare_block/strict.d: Compare the blocks specified by the given vectors and push whether they appear to be identical. Two placed [Edified Stairs](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/edified@hexcasting:cut_edified_plank_variants) will only compare as equal if they appear exactly the same.

hexcasting:compare_entity.d: Compare the given entities and push whether they are of the same type.

hexcasting:compare_item/lenient.d: Compare the items represented or held by the given entities and push whether they are the same type of item. Two [Foci](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/focus) will always compare as equal.

hexcasting:compare_item/strict.d: Like [Sorter's Distillation](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/types@hexcasting:compare_item/lenient), but push whether they are identical items. Two [Foci](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/focus) only compare as identical if they hold the same iota and have [the same appearance](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/spells/cyclevariant).

hexcasting:append.d: Remove the top of the stack, then add it to the end of the list at the top of the stack. | Remove the iota at the top of the stack, then add it to the set. The iota's type must match the set's type.

hexcasting:unappend.d: Remove the iota on the end of the list at the top of the stack, and add it to the top of the stack.

hexcasting:index.d: Remove the number at the top of the stack, then replace the list at the top with the nth element of that list (where n is the number you removed). Replaces the list with Null if the number is out of bounds. | Pushes the nth glyph in the text.

hexcasting:for_each.d: Remove something evaluatable and a list from the stack, then cast the evaluatable over each element of the list.

hexcasting:singleton.d: Remove the top of the stack, then push a list containing only that element.

hexcasting:empty_list.d: Push an empty list to the top of the stack.

hexcasting:reverse.d: Reverse the list at the top of the stack. | Accepts an n by m matrix and returns an m by n matrix where every entry has been flipped along the diagonal. | Reverses the text.

hexcasting:last_n_list.d: Remove *num* elements from the stack, then add them to a list at the top of the stack.

hexcasting:splat.d: Remove the list at the top of the stack, then push its contents to the stack. | Remove the Jump iota at the top of the stack, then, for each of its frames, push a new Jump iota containing only that frame to the stack.

hexcasting:index_of.d: Remove the iota at the top of the stack, then replace the list at the top with the first index of that iota within the list (starting from 0). Replaces the list with -1 if the iota doesn't exist in the list. | Pushes the value present at the provided key, or [Null](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/consts@hexcasting:const/null) if no value was present. | Remove the iota top of the stack, then return True if the set contains that iota, otherwise return False. The iota's type must match the set's type. | Removes two strings from the top of the stack, and returns the first index of the first string where the second string is a substring.
hexcasting:index_of.i: list, any | dict, key | set, (num|vec|entity) | str, str

hexcasting:remove_from.d: Remove the number at the top of the stack, then remove the nth element of the list at the top of the stack (where n is the number you removed). | Removes the key-value pair from the Dictionary, pushing the previous value, or [Null](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/consts@hexcasting:const/null) if no value was present. | Remove the iota from top of the stack, then remove it set. The iota's type must match the set's type. | Removes the nth glyph in the text.
hexcasting:remove_from.i: list, num | dict, key | set, (num|vec|entity) | text, number

hexcasting:slice.d: Remove the two numbers at the top of the stack, then take a sublist of the list at the top of the stack between those indices, lower bound inclusive, upper bound exclusive. For example, the 0, 2 sublist of [0, 1, 2, 3, 4] would be [0, 1]. | Removes a string and two positive integers from the top of the stack, and returns the substring from the first to the second (inclusive first, exclusive second). | Pushes the specified slice of the text.
hexcasting:slice.i: list, num, num | str, num, num | text, number, number

hexcasting:replace.d: Remove the top iota of the stack and the number at the top, then set the nth element of the list at the top of the stack to that iota (where n is the number you removed). Does nothing if the number is out of bounds. | Places the iota in the Dictionary at the specified key. Not every iota type is allowed to be used as a key, with notable the exceptions being [Garbage](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#casting/101) and [Jump](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/meta@hexcasting:eval/cc) iota. Attempting to set the value of a key to [Null](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/consts@hexcasting:const/null) will remove the key the same way using [Excisor's Distillation](https://real-septicake.github.io/HexThings/v/0.1.8+1.20.1/1.2/en_us#patterns/dict@hexcasting:remove_from) would. | Replaces the glyph at the nth position in the text with another segment of text. Replacement can be longer than one glyph.
hexcasting:replace.i: list, num, any | dict, key, any | text, number, text

hexcasting:construct.d: Remove the top iota, then add it as the first element to the list at the top of the stack. | Remove the Jump iota at the top of the stack, then add its top frame to the top of the Jump iota at the top of the stack.

hexcasting:deconstruct.d: Remove the first iota from the list at the top of the stack, then push that iota to the stack. | Remove the top frame from the Jump iota at the top of the stack, then push a new Jump iota containing only that frame to the stack.

hexcasting:interop/pehkui/get.d: Get the scale of the entity, as a proportion of their normal size. For most entities, this will be 1.

hexcasting:interop/pehkui/set.d: Set the scale of the entity, passing in a proportion of their normal size. Costs about 1 Amethyst Shard.

caduceus:eval/prompt.d: Cast a pattern or list of patterns from the stack exactly like [Hermes' Gambit](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/meta@hexcasting:eval), except that anything outside of this cast will not be captured by an [Arke's Gambit](https://caduceus.hexxy.media/v/0.3.0+1.20.1/1.0/en_us#caduceus/patterns/delimcc@caduceus:eval/control) within it.

caduceus:eval/prompt_at.d: Like [Thetis' Gambit](https://caduceus.hexxy.media/v/0.3.0+1.20.1/1.0/en_us#caduceus/patterns/delimcc@caduceus:eval/prompt), but also sets the [jump tag](https://caduceus.hexxy.media/v/0.3.0+1.20.1/1.0/en_us#caduceus/patterns/jump_manipulation@jump_tags) of the cast to the given iota. If the iota is [Null](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#casting/101), this is equivalent to [Thetis' Gambit](https://caduceus.hexxy.media/v/0.3.0+1.20.1/1.0/en_us#caduceus/patterns/delimcc@caduceus:eval/prompt).

caduceus:eval/control.d: Cast a pattern or list of patterns from the stack similarly to [Iris' Gambit](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/meta@hexcasting:eval/cc). Must be drawn within [Thetis' Gambit](https://caduceus.hexxy.media/v/0.3.0+1.20.1/1.0/en_us#caduceus/patterns/delimcc@caduceus:eval/prompt).

caduceus:eval/control_at.d: Like [Arke's Gambit](https://caduceus.hexxy.media/v/0.3.0+1.20.1/1.0/en_us#caduceus/patterns/delimcc@caduceus:eval/control), but only patterns within an enclosing [Thetis' Gambit II](https://caduceus.hexxy.media/v/0.3.0+1.20.1/1.0/en_us#caduceus/patterns/delimcc@caduceus:eval/prompt_at) with a [jump tag](https://caduceus.hexxy.media/v/0.3.0+1.20.1/1.0/en_us#caduceus/patterns/jump_manipulation@jump_tags) matching the given iota are captured. If the iota is [Null](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#casting/101), this is equivalent to [Arke's Gambit](https://caduceus.hexxy.media/v/0.3.0+1.20.1/1.0/en_us#caduceus/patterns/delimcc@caduceus:eval/control).

caduceus:eval/setup_goto.d: Cast a list of patterns from the stack exactly like [Hermes' Gambit](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/meta@hexcasting:eval), except that a [Prometheus' Gambit](https://caduceus.hexxy.media/v/0.3.0+1.20.1/1.0/en_us#caduceus/patterns/goto@caduceus:eval/goto) within this cast will jump to an index within this list of patterns.

caduceus:eval/goto.d: Remove a number from the stack, then jump to that index in the list cast by the enclosing [Elbrus' Gambit](https://caduceus.hexxy.media/v/0.3.0+1.20.1/1.0/en_us#caduceus/patterns/goto@caduceus:eval/setup_goto). If the number is negative, the index counts from the end of the list instead.

caduceus:read/mark/iota.d: Like [Ewer's Reflection](https://caduceus.hexxy.media/v/0.3.0+1.20.1/1.0/en_us#caduceus/patterns/jump_manipulation@caduceus:read/mark/local), but the iota is read out of the jump tag of the top frame in a Jump iota.

caduceus:read/mark/local.d: Copy the iota stored in the jump tag of the current evaluation and add it to the stack.

caduceus:write/mark/local.d:
Remove the top iota from the stack, and write it to the jump tag of the current evaluation.
As with [Chronicler's Gambit](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/readwrite@hexcasting:write/entity), I cannot write my own Name using this spell.

complexhex:conjugate.d: Negates the imaginary coefficient of the topmost iota

complexhex:qinvert.d: Negates the coefficients of i, j, & k

complexhex:qmake.d: Pushes a Quaternion with num as the real coefficient and the vector's x, y, & z as the coefficients of i, j & k respectively.

complexhex:qunmake.d: Pushes the real coefficient and a vector where the x, y, & z components are the coefficients of i, j, & k respectively.

complexhex:quattomat.d: Pushes a matrix that (should) represent the same rotation as the quaternion

complexhex:mattoquat.d: Pushes a quaternion that (should) reperesent the same rotation as the matrix

complexhex:axisangle.d: Pushes a quaternion that reperesents a rotation by the given angle num radias around the given vector.

complexhex:translatebit.d: Translates the BIT to the given offset.

complexhex:rotatebit.d: Rotates the BIT to the given Quaternion.

complexhex:scalebit.d: Scales the BIT to the given vector.

complexhex:get_bit_4x4.d: Pushes a 4x4 matrix representing the Bit's Transformation.

complexhex:set_bit_4x4.d: Sets the Transformation of a BIT to the given 4x4 matrix.

complexhex:get_entity/bit.d: Transform the position on the stack into the BIT at that location (or [Null](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#casting/101) if there isn't one)

complexhex:zone_entity/bit.d: Take a position and a maximum distance on the stack, and combine them into a list of BIT's near the position.

complexhex:zone_entity/not_bit.d: Take a position and a maximum distance on the stack, and combine them into a list of non-BIT's near the position.

complexhex:bubble.d: Pushes a Bubbled Iota, which when popped via execution (by Hermes' or the likes), will push the contained iota to the stack.

complexhex:ascii.d:
Swaps between a string of a *single character* and an integer representing that character.
Uses the UTF-16 character map.

complexhex:long/convert.d:
Converts between [doubles](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/numbers) and longs
Always truncates the value when converting to long

complexhex:shift/left.d: Shifts all the bits to the left num times

complexhex:shift/right/logical.d: Shifts all the bits to the right num times

complexhex:shift/right/arithmetic.d: Shifts all the bits to the right num times while preserving the sign

complexhex:new_symbol.d: Creates a new symbol with the given (single character) label

complexhex:substitute.d: Substitutes the third expression/number in place of the second expression within the first.

complexhex:equals.d: Creates an expression that equals 1 if the two expressions are equal, and 0 otherwise.

complexhex:piecewise.d: Creates a piecewise expression that simplifies to the second argument if the first simplifies to 1.0, otherwise simplifies to the third argument.

complexhex:derivative.d: Takes in an expression and a lone symbol and returns the partial derivative of the expression with respect to the symbol.

complexhex:matrix.d: Takes in a width, height and expression and creates a matrix by substituting i & j-values into the expression corresponding to a position in the matrix and putting the result in the matrix.

complexhex:summon/line.d: Summons a parametric line at the given position. The expression given will have a t-value (0-1), x/y/z position, and time (w) substituted in and must resolve to a vector on the line.

complexhex:summon/surface.d: Summons a parametric surface at the given position. The expression given will have a u&v-value (0-1), x/y/z position, and time (w) substituted in and must resolve to a vector on the surface

complexhex:sinh.d: Evaluates the hyperbolic sine of the argument

complexhex:cosh.d: Evaluates the hyperbolic sine of the argument

complexhex:tanh.d: Evaluates the hyperbolic sine of the argument

complexhex:asinh.d: Evaluates the hyperbolic sine of the argument

complexhex:acosh.d: Evaluates the hyperbolic sine of the argument

complexhex:atanh.d: Evaluates the hyperbolic sine of the argument

dthexcasting:get_species.d: Provided a tree's position, I can extract the Species of the tree.

dthexcasting:get_jocode.d: Provided a tree's position, I can extract the structure of the tree as a Base64 string.

ephemera:removestatus.d: Accepts an entity and a status effect type, and removes that status effect from the entity. Cost is based on the effect's innate harmfulness, its potency, and its remaining duration.

ephemera:getstatus.d: Accepts a living entity, and returns a list of status iotas representing all effects on the target.

ephemera:getstatuscategory.d: Accepts a status effect type, and returns a number based on whether the effect is likely to be helpful, harmful, or neutral to a creature.

ephemera:getstatusduration.d: Accepts an entity and a status effect type, and returns the effect on the target's duration in seconds.

ephemera:getstatuslevel.d: Accepts an entity and a status effect type, and returns the effect on the target's potency.

ephemera:getbystatus.d: Accepts a status effect type, a vector, and a number (*n*), and returns a list of entities within radius *n* of the vector which have that effect.

ephemera:getbystatusinverse.d: Accepts a status effect type, a vector, and a number (*n*), and returns a list of entities within radius *n* of the vector which do not have that effect.

ephemera:getbystatussingle.d: Accepts a status effect type and a vector, and returns an entity at that position which has that effect.

ephemera:getabsorption.d: Accepts a living entity, and returns how much damage it can Absorb before its health is affected.

ephemera:filteredentityraycast.d: As [Scout's Distillation](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/basics@hexcasting:raycast/entity), but also accepts a list of entity type iotas. Any entity whose type is not present in the list will be ignored. Costs an amount of media slightly less negligible than that of the aforementioned pattern.

ephemera:gaussianrand.d: Returns a random number with a gaussian distribution, with a mean of zero and a standard deviation of one.

ephemera:hash.d: Accepts any iota, and converts it into its hashed form.

ephemera:getrevealcost.d: Accepts a player and returns how much amethyst dust it would cost to send them a message via Postman's Gambit, between 1/10 of a dust and 10 dust.

ephemera:getdurabilitymainhand.d: Returns how many times the item in my other hand can be used without breaking, durability-manipulating effects notwithstanding.

ephemera:getdurabilityoffhand.d: As previous, targeting the item in the hand I'm casting this with. Most useful with delayed casts of one form or another.

ephemera:getiotasize.d: Accepts any iota, and returns its total size.

ephemera:getstacksizedeep.d: Returns the total size of all iotas on my stack, including the contents of lists and similar. If this number ever reaches 1024, my stack shall come crashing down into garbage.

ephemera:collisionprobe.d: Accepts a vector, and returns whether that vector is within (or just on the edge of) the block in that space. Seems to involve the boxes I see in my mind's eye.

ephemera:thothyoink.d: Pops an iota from the accumulator and pushes it to the current stack. Mishaps if used outside of Thoth's Gambit.

ephemera:thothcount.d: Returns how many iotas are currently accessible via Seshat's Gambit. Returns -1 if used outside of Thoth's Gambit.

ephemera:getproperties.d: Accepts a vector, and returns a list of strings corresponding to values contained in the state of the block at the corresponding position.

ephemera:getpropertyvalue.d: Accepts a vector and a string, and uses the string as a key to retrieve the value it corresponds to in the target block's state, or null if there is no corresponding value.

ephemera:getrider.d: Accepts an entity, and returns a list of entities seated atop it.

ephemera:getmount.d: Accepts an entity, and returns the entity it is seated atop.

ephemera:getflight/type.d: Returns true if the target is under the effects of Anchorite's Flight, false if Wayfarer's Flight, null if neither.

ephemera:getflight/remaining.d: Returns how close the target is to the end of their flight spell, represented as either their distance to the boundary or how many seconds remain.

ephemera:readframerotation.d: Accepts an item frame entity, and returns its rotation, from 0 to 7.

ephemera:setframerotation.d: Accepts an item frame entity and an integer from 0 to 7, and sets its rotation to the number. Costs a negligible amount of media.

ephemera:networkscan.d: Scans the link network connected to the input linkable up to a recursion depth equal to the input number (max 32), and returns a list of all connected linkables. Costs a negligible amount of media.

ephemera:networkindex.d: Accepts a linkable to use for network access, and any iota. If a relay connected to the network has an adjacent Network Routing Index with the same iota, returns that relay's position. Costs half an amethyst dust.

ephemera:networktp.d: Accepts an entity to teleport, a linkable to use for access to its network, and a destination. If the entity is within 8 blocks of the linkable, and there is a network node within 4 blocks of the destination, the entity will be teleported. Cost varies based on what entity is teleported.

ephemera:particleburst.d: Accepts two vectors and two numbers, and uses them to define a burst of particles. Costs a negligible amount of media.

ephemera:paintconjured.d: Accepts a vector and an itemtype representing a pigment. Costs a negligible amount of media if targeting my own block, or 1 Amethyst Dust if not.

ephemera:revealtoother.d: Accepts a player and any iota less than 256 characters long, and shows that iota to them as if they had cast Reveal, also telling them who sent the message. Cost is inversely proportional to the length of time since they were last targeted by this spell.

ephemera:clearrevealcost.d: Resets the cost of sending me a message via Postman's Gambit back to 1/10 of a dust. Costs 1/10 of a dust.

ephemera:ridewisp.d: Accepts one of my wisps (or a wandering wisp), and places me atop it, similar to sitting in a minecart. I must be within the wisp's ambit, or four blocks for wandering wisps. Costs one amethyst shard.

ephemera:dismount.d: Takes me off of whatever entity I may be riding when cast. Costs 1/100 of a dust.

ephemera:cancelflight.d: Cancels my current flight ability, at a cost of one tenth of an Amethyst Dust. Casting a new flight spell in the same instant allows me to continue flying, potentially with different parameters.

focalworks:rig_read.d: Takes in an item entity and a hex, and rigs the item's read to that hex.

focalworks:rig_write.d: Takes in an item entity and a hex, and rigs the item's write to that hex.

focalworks:crack_rig.d: Takes in an item entity and cracks the focus.

focalworks:flip_spellbook.d: This pattern takes in a spellbook item entity and a num, and flips the spellbook to that page.

focalworks:read_spellbook_page.d: This pattern takes in a spellbook item entity and returns the currently selected page.

focalworks:rig_write_index.d: Rigs the write from [Tachygrapher's Gambit](https://ioticblocks.hexxy.media/v/1.0.2+1.20.1/1.0/en_us#patterns/readwrite_blocks@ioticblocks:write/index) with the given hex.

focalworks:rig_read_index.d: Rigs the read from [Tachygrapher's Distillation](https://ioticblocks.hexxy.media/v/1.0.2+1.20.1/1.0/en_us#patterns/readwrite_blocks@ioticblocks:read/index) with the given hex.

hexkeys:library.d: It started with a crack... A small thing really. I felt a light breeze from it that told me things. I'm now certain that every mind has some form of physical representation. I just need to get there. If only I could push that crack wider...

hexkeys:visit_library.d: I should also keep in mind that this method only seems to work on those like myself. Those of us who have "opened" our minds to the realm around us.

hexkeys:read_noetic_bookshelf.d: Read the content of a noetic shelf onto the stack.

hexkeys:get_noetic_bookshelf_ref.d: Adds a reference to a noetic bookshelf to the stack. This reference may be used for targeting in place of a vector for noetic spells

hexkeys:concat_noetic_bookshelf.d: Concatenate a list onto the end of a noetic shelf

hexkeys:erase_noetic_bookshelf.d: Erase a noetic bookshelf, this allows you to re-write a shelf from scratch

hexways:summonscry.d: Works as a 1-way portal, but does not provide travel, only sight. Costs increase with distance, though noticeably less than for other portals.

hexways:moveportalinput.d: Takes a portal and location vector, and moves its input to that location. The cost is slightly lesser than portal creation, and is reduced for scrying portals.

hexways:moveportaloutput.d: Takes a portal and location vector, and moves its output to that location. For a two-way portal, this also moves the portal on the other side, as expected. Costs are similar to the previous pattern.

hexways:rotateportal.d: Ah, fickle rotation vectors. To my luck, I may use this spell to change the rotation of a given portal. The final argument determines whether the rotation is limited to one side, for a 2-way portal.

hexways:setportalsides.d: As, well, *familiar* as I am with hexagons, sadly they don't fit every situation. But with this spell, I may alter the count of a portal's sides and roll, free of cost.

hexways:removeportal.d: Alas, if a portal provides the visage of too much for my eyes to handle, this spell may cut the string, banishing a portal pair. Costs no media.

hexways:resizeportal.d: Passing a portal, height, and width, I may change the size of the portal, reverting it to a hexagonal shape, curiously. Costs no media.

hexways:getoutputinfo.d: This nifty pattern returns a portal's output location as a vector (which will be the location of the output portal, for a 2-way portal). This could be useful combined with Portal Ambit. Costs no media.

hex_ars_link:cast_spell.d:
Cast the given spell from myself.
Costs 1 dust for each glyph used.

hex_ars_link:cast_spell_shoot.d:
Cast the given spell as a projectile shooting from certain position & angle. One Glyph of Projectile will be inserted before the given glyphs.
Costs 1 shard plus 1 dust for each glyph used.

hex_ars_link:cast_spell_touch.d:
Cast the given spell on given entity or position. One Glyph of Touch will be inserted before the given glyphs.
Costs 1 shard plus 1 dust for each glyph used.

hex_ars_link:read_glyphs.d:
Read all glyphs from a given entity: could be an item like glyph, spellcaster and parchment, or item frames containing those, or a player with learnt glyphs.
This could be the only way to obtain a glyph iota if I choose to deny the evil power of HexParse.

hex_ars_link:set_callback.d: Register the given spell list as callback, which will be executed when "Trigger Callback" glyph executes.

hex_ars_link:get_callback.d: Read the callback spell list registered.

hex_ars_link:query_mana.d: Gets how many points of current mana I have.

hex_ars_link:query_mana_max.d: Gets how many points of mana I could have at most.

hexautomata:quantum_swap.d: Swaps me and the triggering entity spatially, at cost of half of a dust. Takes no effect if there's no such entity (for example, hurt event triggered by environmental damage).

hexautomata:event/write.d: Write given iota into the Reactive Focus triggering. Might be helpful if one wants to look into self more thoroughly.

hexautomata:event/read.d: Reads the spell currently running during the event from certain Reactive Focus. Might be helpful if one wants to look into self more thoroughly.

hexdebug:const/cognitohazard.d: Add a Cognitohazard to the top of the stack.

hexdebug:const/debugging.d: Add True to the top of the stack if executed by a [Debugger](https://hexdebug.hexxy.media/v/0.8.1+1.20.1/1.1/en_us#items/debugging@debugger) or [Evaluator](https://hexdebug.hexxy.media/v/0.8.1+1.20.1/1.1/en_us#items/debugging@evaluator), or False otherwise.

hexdebug:breakpoint/before.d: Pause the [Debugger](https://hexdebug.hexxy.media/v/0.8.1+1.20.1/1.1/en_us#items/debugging@debugger) before executing this pattern.

hexdebug:breakpoint/after.d: Pause the [Debugger](https://hexdebug.hexxy.media/v/0.8.1+1.20.1/1.1/en_us#items/debugging@debugger) after executing this pattern (ie. before executing the next pattern).

hexdebug:craft/debugger.d:
Create a [Debugger](https://hexdebug.hexxy.media/v/0.8.1+1.20.1/1.1/en_us#items/debugging@debugger) that casts a Hex, similar to [certain other patterns](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/spells/hexcasting) I've used in the past.
Costs about ten [Charged Amethyst](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hexdebug:craft/quenched_debugger.d:
Create a [Quenched Debugger](https://hexdebug.hexxy.media/v/0.8.1+1.20.1/1.1/en_us#greatwork/quenching_debuggers) that casts a Hex, similar to [certain other patterns](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/spells/hexcasting) I've used in the past.
Costs about ten [Charged Amethyst](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hexdebug:splicing/selection/read.d: Remove a vector from the stack, then push two values representing the current selection in the [Splicing Table](https://hexdebug.hexxy.media/v/0.8.1+1.20.1/1.1/en_us#items/splicing_table) at that position.

hexdebug:splicing/selection/write.d: Remove a vector and two values from the stack, then set the selection of the [Splicing Table](https://hexdebug.hexxy.media/v/0.8.1+1.20.1/1.1/en_us#items/splicing_table) at that position as previously described.

hexdebug:splicing/view_index/read.d: Remove a vector from the stack, then push the index of the leftmost iota currently visible in the [Splicing Table](https://hexdebug.hexxy.media/v/0.8.1+1.20.1/1.1/en_us#items/splicing_table) at that position.

hexdebug:splicing/view_index/write.d: Remove a vector and number from the stack, then move the view of the [Splicing Table](https://hexdebug.hexxy.media/v/0.8.1+1.20.1/1.1/en_us#items/splicing_table) at that position so that the given index is the leftmost one visible.

hexdebug:splicing/list/spellbook_index/r.d: Remove a vector from the stack, then push the current page number (starting at 1) of the [Spellbook](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/spellbook) in the main slot of the [Splicing Table](https://hexdebug.hexxy.media/v/0.8.1+1.20.1/1.1/en_us#items/splicing_table) or [Focal Frame](https://hexdebug.hexxy.media/v/0.8.1+1.20.1/1.1/en_us#items/focus_holder) at that position.

hexdebug:splicing/list/spellbook_index/w.d: Remove a vector and number from the stack, then flip the [Spellbook](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/spellbook) in the main slot of the [Splicing Table](https://hexdebug.hexxy.media/v/0.8.1+1.20.1/1.1/en_us#items/splicing_table) or [Focal Frame](https://hexdebug.hexxy.media/v/0.8.1+1.20.1/1.1/en_us#items/focus_holder) at that position to the given page number.

hexdebug:splicing/list/spellbook_index/r.d: Replace the vector at the top of the stack with True if there is a [Splicing Table](https://hexdebug.hexxy.media/v/0.8.1+1.20.1/1.1/en_us#items/splicing_table) or [Focal Frame](https://hexdebug.hexxy.media/v/0.8.1+1.20.1/1.1/en_us#items/focus_holder) at that position with a [Spellbook](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/spellbook) in its main slot that contains at least one page, or False otherwise.

hexdebug:splicing/clipboard/read.d: Remove a vector from the stack, then copy the contents of the secondary item in the [Splicing Table](https://hexdebug.hexxy.media/v/0.8.1+1.20.1/1.1/en_us#items/splicing_table) at that position and push it to the stack.

hexdebug:splicing/clipboard/write.d:
Remove a vector and iota from the stack, then save the iota into the secondary item in the [Splicing Table](https://hexdebug.hexxy.media/v/0.8.1+1.20.1/1.1/en_us#items/splicing_table) at that position.
As with [Chronicler's Gambit](https://ioticblocks.hexxy.media/v/1.0.2+1.20.1/1.0/en_us#patterns/readwrite_blocks@hexcasting:write/entity), I cannot write my own Name using this spell.

hexdebug:splicing/clipboard/readable.d: Replace the vector at the top of the stack with True if there is a [Splicing Table](https://hexdebug.hexxy.media/v/0.8.1+1.20.1/1.1/en_us#items/splicing_table) at that position containing a secondary item that I could read, or False otherwise.

hexdebug:splicing/clipboard/writable.d: Replace the vector at the top of the stack with True if there is a [Splicing Table](https://hexdebug.hexxy.media/v/0.8.1+1.20.1/1.1/en_us#items/splicing_table) at that position containing a secondary item that I could save an iota into, or False otherwise.

hexdebug:splicing/clipboard/spellbook_in.d: Like [Projectionist's Purification](https://hexdebug.hexxy.media/v/0.8.1+1.20.1/1.1/en_us#patterns/splicing_table@hexdebug:splicing/list/spellbook_index/read), but the page number of the [Spellbook](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/spellbook) in the secondary slot is read instead of the main slot.

Like [Projectionist's Gambit](https://hexdebug.hexxy.media/v/0.8.1+1.20.1/1.1/en_us#patterns/splicing_table@hexdebug:splicing/list/spellbook_index/write), but the page number of the [Spellbook](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/spellbook) in the secondary slot is written instead of the main slot.

Like [Shutter's Purification](https://hexdebug.hexxy.media/v/0.8.1+1.20.1/1.1/en_us#patterns/splicing_table@hexdebug:splicing/list/spellbook_index/readable), but the [Spellbook](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/spellbook) in the secondary slot is checked instead of the main slot.

hexdebug:splicing/enlightened/hex/read.d: Remove a vector from the stack, then push the Hex currently imbued to the [Mindsplice Table](https://hexdebug.hexxy.media/v/0.8.1+1.20.1/1.1/en_us#greatwork/enlightened_splicing_table) at that position, or [Null](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#casting/101) if it has not yet been imbued.

hexdebug:splicing/enlightened/hex/write.d:
Remove a vector and list of patterns from the stack, then imbue the list of patterns into the [Mindsplice Table](https://hexdebug.hexxy.media/v/0.8.1+1.20.1/1.1/en_us#greatwork/enlightened_splicing_table) at that position.
Costs about five [Charged Amethyst](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hexflow:pure_map.d: Similar to [Thoth's Gambit](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/meta@hexcasting:for_each), but won't copy the original stack inside each sub-execution.

hexflow:pure_reduce.d: Similar to [Thoth's Gambit](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/meta@hexcasting:for_each); for data list with length **n**, it executes **n - 1** times; The first initial stack is the first two elements, and each subsequent execution uses the stack after the last execution.

hexflow:for_range/cube.d: Executes given list on each point as initial iota inside the cuboid defined by given 2 points as body diagonal.

hexflow:for_range/cube/pure.d:
...and yes, there are pure version for those shaped mapping patterns, too.
Everything the same, except that original stack isn't copied into each sub-executions.

hexflow:for_range/line.d: Executes given list on each point as initial iota on the line connecting 2 points (start, end).

hexflow:for_range/line/pure.d: Everything the same, except that original stack isn't copied into each sub-executions.

hexflow:inf_loop.d:
*(technically not a Thoth but...)*
Consumes and executes given executable on current stack **INFINITELY, UNTIL THE END.**

hexflow:fsm.d:
*(technically not a Thoth but...)*
Takes eval-ables list as **states**. Each iteration, pops int **n** and executes **states[n]**. Stops if stack top is not a valid state index.

hexflow:build_nested.d: Copy list #0 and set back to index #1

hexflow:nested_modify.d: List iota #0 is the nested list to be modified. According to the index sequence given by list #1, traverses to the inner layer, and sets the corresponding element to iota #2.

hexflow:mass_rotate.d: Accepts the size to reorder and a bottom-to-top order list, and do the corresponding reorder to the rest of the stack. For example, **3** plus **[1,2,0]** for [Rotation Gambit](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/stackmanip@hexcasting:rotate), and **2** plus **[0,1,0,1]** for [Dioscuri Gambit](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/stackmanip@hexcasting:2dup)

hexflow:weak_escape.d: Same as [Consideration](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/patterns_as_iotas@hexcasting:escape), but with lowest execution priority, and won't grow in **2^n** formula exponentially inside nested [Intro-Retro](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/patterns_as_iotas@hexcasting:open_paren)s

hexflow:call_stack.d: Executes given pattern/list/Jump? iota in an independent stack, then recovers the original stack at bottom. If given an integer argument X no more than stack size, first X iotas will be taken away as the initial new stack.

hexgender:female_transition.d:
Transitions the caster to a female!
I wonder how I'd look in a skirt...

hexgender:male_transition.d:
Transitions the caster to a male!
No more periods!

hexgender:other_transition.d:
Transitions the caster to androgynous!
Hmm... this is... interesting...

hexgender:get_gender.d: Obtains the target's selected gender as an ordinal (number)

hexgender:get_bust_size.d: Gives the bust size of the target

hexgender:set_bust_size.d: Sets the bust size of the caster

hexgender:get_bounciness.d: Gives the bounciness of the target's breasts

hexgender:set_bounciness.d: Sets the bounciness of the caster's breasts

hexgender:get_floppiness.d: Gives the floppiness of the target's breasts

hexgender:set_floppiness.d: Sets the floppiness of the caster's breasts

hexgender:get_physics.d: Gives the physics of the target's breasts

hexgender:set_physics.d: Sets the physics of the caster's breasts

hexgender:get_cleavage.d: Gets the cleavage of the target's breasts

hexgender:set_cleavage.d: Sets the cleavage of the caster's breasts

hexgender:get_breast_offsets.d: Gets the offset of the target's breasts

hexgender:set_breast_offsets.d: Sets the offset of the caster's breasts

hexgender:get_uniboob.d: Gets whether the target's breasts are a uniboob

hexgender:set_uniboob.d: Sets whether the caster's breasts are a uniboob

manifestation:create_list_menu.d: Takes a list of intents, a menu title and manifests a list menu.

manifestation:create_grid_menu.d: Takes a list of intents, a menu title, and a number of columns to manifest a grid menu. Columns are limited to 1-10.

manifestation:create_radial_menu.d: Takes a list of intents and a menu title to manifest a radial button menu. Radial menus only accept button intents

manifestation:intent_button.d: Creates a button from a list of patterns and a label. When clicked, the button casts the patterns. The patterns are cast in their own environment so they can't use special patterns specific to spell circles or charms. They inherit the stack of environment they are cast from.

manifestation:intent_input.d: Creates an input field from a label. Entered text is pushed to the stack of an executed action, like from a button.

manifestation:intent_numeric_input.d: Creates a numeric input from a default value and label. The entered number is pushed to the stack of an executed action.

manifestation:intent_slider.d: Creates a slider from min, max, current values, and a label. The chosen value is pushed to the stack of an executed action.

manifestation:intent_checkbox.d: Creates a checkbox from a default checked state and label. The resulting boolean is pushed to the stack of an executed action.

manifestation:intent_select_list.d: Creates a selectable list from options, a max visible row count, and a label. Optionally accepts a boolean to enable multi-select. The selected option or options are pushed to the stack of an executed action.

manifestation:intent_section.d: Creates a non-interactive section from a label, acting as a sub heading.

manifestation:intent_dropdown.d: Creates a dropdown from a list of options and a label. The selected option is pushed to the stack of an executed action.

manifestation:link_intent_relay.d: Takes a destination vector for where the relay will go, then a face vector to choose which side to manifest it on, and then a target vector for the thing to link the relay to.

manifestation:open_corridor_portal.d: Takes a vector, a Prescence intent, media allocation and an optional string label and pigment. Opens a portal bridging two locations together.**Cost: 2 dust per second. 35 Charged Crystal on frame.**

manifestation:presence_intent.d: Takes a location and a directional vector and creates an intent. Used with manifest threshold.**Cost: 35 amethyst.**

manifestation:destroy_manifestation.d: Takes an origin vector and a radius, destroys manifestations (portals and relays) in that area. Based on permissions.

manifestation:manifest_splinter.d: Creates a splinter at a position, with a delay and a list of patterns to cast. The splinter casts the payload as if it were the caster, then collapses. The splinter's location is only visible to its creator.

manifestation:destroy_current_splinter.d: Only castable by a splinter. Dismisses only the current splinter.

manifestation:destroy_splinters.d: Dismisses all splinters you have active.

manifestation:get_splinter_location.d: Only castable by a splinter. Returns the current vector of the splinter. Useful for self-renewal.

manifestation:renew_splinter.d: Only castable by a splinter. Renews the current splinter, with the same pattern. Preserves the Ravenmind between splinters.

manifestation:saturns_gambit.d:
Like Hermes' Gambit but executes it asynchronously, splitting up large lists of work over multiple ticks that execute synchronously.
It borrows the technique from Splinters but is not a Splinter.

manifestation:hex_trail.d: Hex Trail creates a particle trail as it moves. By using the same ID across casts you can create a continuous trail that moves smoothy between positions.
manifestation:hex_trail.i: vec, vec, vec, num, num, num?

manifestation:equation_hex_cloud.d: Creates large particle effects from an Equation Particle iota to avoid large vector lists. The Iota can be created using an Equation Synthesizer block. Uses an ID to keep positional state like Hex Trail.

manifestation:spell_circle.d: Projects a solid spell circle into the world displaying a pattern for a duration before disintegrating.**Cost: 1/500 dust.**

manifestation:set_charm_cast_sound.d:
Changes the sound a charmed item makes when casting.
Top of stack is string, text, or null.**Cost: 10 dust.**

manifestation:memory_reflection.d: Returns the held or embedded Memory Crystal's unique memory identifier. Favours the off-hand first.

manifestation:replay_memory.d: Returns the stored memory pattern (or null if none) from a held or embedded Memory Crystal. Takes a Memory Iota from Memory Reflection. Favours the off-hand first.

manifestation:store_memory.d: Stores the top of the stack in a held or embedded Memory Crystal's memory. Takes a Memory Iota from Memory Reflection. Favours the off-hand first.

manifestation:mind_vault_counts.d: Takes a vector of a mind vault location and returns [ready, total], where ready is the number of stored minds not on cooldown and total is the number of stored minds in the vault.

manifestation:exit_if_interacting.d: Exits a hex if caster uses something interactable. Useful for charmed items that use righ-click.

manifestation:open_casting_screen.d: Opens the spell grid and must be cast by a person.

manifestation:clear_stack.d: Clears the caster's persisted staff stack (the shift, right-click stack). Must be cast by a person.

hexmapping:create_marker/circle.d: Creates a new Circle Marker with the provided identifier, label, position, and radius

hexmapping:create_marker/rectangle.d: Creates a new Rectangle Marker with the provided identifier, label, top corner, and bottom corner

hexmapping:create_marker/polygon.d: Creates a new Polygon Marker with the provided identifier, label, and list of positions OR a Hexical Mesh Entity

hexmapping:create_marker/polyline.d: Creates a new Polyline Marker with the provided identifier, label, and list of positions OR a Hexical Mesh Entity

hexmapping:create_marker/icon.d: Creates a new Icon Marker with the provided identifier, label, icon, and position

hexmapping:has_marker.d: Checks if a marker exists on the map under the provided identifier

hexmapping:set_fill_color.d: Sets the Fill Color of a marker, if applicable (Circle, Rectangle, and Polygon)

hexmapping:set_line_color.d: Sets the Line Color of a marker, if applicable (Circle, Rectangle, Polyline, and Polygon)

hexmapping:set_line_weight.d: Sets the Line Weight of a marker, if applicable (Circle, Rectangle, Polyline, and Polygon)

hexmapping:get_maps/bluemap.d: Pushes a list of Maps for your current dimension from Bluemap to the stack

hexmapping:get_maps/dynmap.d: Pushes a list of Maps for your current dimension from Dynmap to the stack

hexmapping:get_maps/pl3xmap.d: Pushes a list of Maps for your current dimension from Pl3xmap to the stack

hexmapping:get_maps/squaremap.d: Pushes a list of Maps for your current dimension from Squaremap to the stack

hexoverpowered:get_personal_media.d: Gets how much media exists in my personal media bar (in **0.0001** dust).

hexoverpowered:get_personal_media_max.d: Gets how much media I could hold in my personal media bar at most (in **0.0001** dust).

hexoverpowered:mind_stack/push.d: Pops the top iota from current stack, and pushes into the staff casting stack.

hexoverpowered:mind_stack/pop.d: Pops the top iota from the staff casting stack, and pushes into current stack.

hexoverpowered:mind_stack/size.d: Gets the size of the staff casting stack.

hexoverpowered:mind_patterns.d: Gets the list of all pattern iotas in the current staff canvas, returned in the order they were drawn.

hexoverpowered:mind_env/schedule.d: Delays **the single** given iota list to execute after the given time (number of ticks). If delay time is not greater than 0, then the spell will be casted immediately.

hexoverpowered:mind_env/running_code.d: Gets the list of patterns executed last time in the current casting environment.

hexparse:code2focus.d:
Reads code from my local clipboard, then parse it into the focus I'm holding.
Can only be casted by staff.

hexparse:focus2code.d:
Reads data from the focus I'm holding, and prints parsed code into chat menu.
Can only be casted by staff.

hexparse:remove_comments.d: Clears all comment iotas in a list, returns processed list.

hexparse:learn_patterns.d: Extract great patterns from handheld items (ancient scrolls, focuses, compiled casting items, etc.), and returns a list of newly learned ones by the parser.
