hexparse:create_linebreak.d: Adds a line-break comment iota with space-indents of given number to the stack.

hexparse:donate.d: Donate a certain amount of media (in dusts) to the Nature.

hexparse:switch_comment.d: Transforms input Comment Iota into String Iota, or everything else into Comment Iota; has no effect if **MoreIotas** not installed.

hexstruction:save_structure.d:
Removes the locations of two corners from the stack, then consumes a region of space defined by those two corners, storing the result in a Structure iota.
Costs about an eighth of one [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst) for every block consumed.

hexstruction:load_structure.d:
Removes the location of the structure's origin and a structure from the stack, then attempts to place the structure at the origin, erasing the structure from all memory. Mishaps if any part of the structure overlaps with another block.
Costs about an eighth of one [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst) for every block placed.

hexstruction:display_structure.d: Removes the location of the structure's origin and a structure from the stack, followed by a duration between 0 and 72000.

hexstruction:mirror_left_right.d: Flips a stored Structure left-to-right, or across the X-axis.

hexstruction:mirror_front_back.d: Flips a stored Structure front-to-back, or across the Z-axis.

hexstruction:mirror_vertical.d: Flips a stored Structure top-to-bottom, or across the Y-axis.

hexstruction:rotate_clockwise.d: Rotates a stored Structure 90-degrees clockwise about the Y-axis.

hexstruction:rotate_counterclockwise.d: Rotates a stored Structure 90-degrees counterclockwise about the Y-axis.

hexstruction:rotate_clockwise_x.d: Rotates a stored Structure 90-degrees clockwise about the X-axis.

hexstruction:rotate_counterclockwise_x.d: Rotates a stored Structure 90-degrees counterclockwise about the X-axis.

hexstruction:rotate_clockwise_z.d: Rotates a stored Structure 90-degrees clockwise about the Z-axis.

hexstruction:rotate_counterclockwise_z.d: Rotates a stored Structure 90-degrees counterclockwise about the Z-axis.

hexstruction:transformations.d: Removes a Structure from the stack, returning its transformations as a list in the format [mirror, vertical mirror, rotationX, rotationY, rotationZ].

hexthings:insert.d: Similar to [Surgeon's Exaltation](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/lists@hexcasting:replace), but replaces the element of the first list instead with the *contents* of the second list, rather than with the list itself.

hexthings:requote.d: When used after an [Introjection](https://real-septicake.github.io/HexThings/v/0.1.8+1.20.1/1.2/en_us#patterns/hexutils@hexthings:unquote), This pattern puts all iota on the stack into the escaped list, with the previous state of the stack being restored.

hexthings:isgreatersent.d: Pushes if my current sentinel is a [Greater Sentinel](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/great_spells/greater_sentinel), or [Null](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/consts@hexcasting:const/null) if I have no sentinel at all.

hexthings:dict_keys.d: Pushes a list of the keys present in the Dictionary.

hexthings:dict_vals.d: Pushes a list of the values present in the Dictionary.

hexthings:dict_ents.d: Pushes a list of the key-value pairs in this Dictionary, each being a 2 element list.

hexthings:uiua_take.d: Keeps elements of the list based on the second argument. If it's a number and positive, it keeps the first *n* elements of the list, if negative; the last *n*. If given a list, then its elements are treated as indices to keep.

hexthings:uiua_drop.d: The exact inverse of [Retention Distillation](https://real-septicake.github.io/HexThings/v/0.1.8+1.20.1/1.2/en_us#patterns/uiua@hexthings:uiua_take), dropping the specified elements instead of dropping the rest.

hexthings:uiua_rotate.d: Shifts the contents of the list by the specified amount, wrapping elements that go "outside" the list.

hexthings:uiua_where.d: Pushes a list containing the indices of values that are [considered true by Nature](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/logic@hexcasting:bool_coerce).

hexthings:make_range.d: Creates a list from num #1 to num #2, with a step size of num #3 (or 1 if passed null). For example, A stack of [1, 2, 0.5] would result in a list of [1, 1.5].

hextweaks:page/right.d: Turns the spellbook that your are holding one page to the right

hextweaks:page/left.d: Turns the spellbook that your are holding one page to the left

hextweaks:while.d: Removes a pattern list from the stack. Examines (but does not remove) the iota beneath it, and evaluates the pattern list if and only if [Augur's Purification](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/logic@hexcasting:bool_coerce) would respond to that iota with True. Examination and evaluation repeats until the iota would no longer create truth.

hextweaks:wave.d: Returns the posistion of the Wave of media passing through a [Spell Circle](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#greatwork/impetus)

hextweaks:normal.d: Returns the normal of the slate the Wave is on in the [Spell Circle](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#greatwork/impetus)

hexweb:parse_json.d: Turns the given String into a JSON object. If it cannot be parsed into a JSON object itself, a wrapper JSON object will be created.

hexweb:set_element.d: Sets the given iota at the given key. Setting a Garbage iota removes the key.

hexweb:get_element.d: Gets the stored iota at the given key. Mishaps upon their being no iota.

hexweb:has_element.d: Checks whether the given JSON iota has the given key.

hexweb:request.d:
Sends an HTTP request made of the given data, method, and headers to the provided URL.
The Response is truthy if a response is received.

hexweb:get_response.d: Given a Response Iota, attempt to parse the results. Will Mishap if too early or an IOException is thrown.

hexal:current_tick.d: Adds a number to the stack which seems to be related to how Nature represents time; If I cast the pattern, then cast the same pattern a second later, the number it adds has increased by 20.

hexal:breath.d: Removes a Living entity from the stack and returns how much breath it has left (i.e., how close it is to drowning).

hexal:health.d: Removes a Living entity from the stack and returns how much health it has left (i.e., how close it is to dying).

hexal:armour.d: Removes a Living entity from the stack and returns how much armour it has.

hexal:toughness.d: Removes a Living entity from the stack and returns how much toughness it has (another property of armour).

hexal:light_level.d: Removes a position vector from the stack and returns the light level at that position.

hexal:factorial.d: Takes a number from the stack and computes its factorial, for example inputting 4 would return 4\*3\*2\*1=24.

hexal:running/sum.d: Takes a list from the stack and computes its running sum, for example inputting [1,2,5] would return [1,3,8].

hexal:running/mul.d: Takes a list from the stack and computes its running product, for example inputting [1,2,5] would return [1,2,10].

hexal:everbook/read.d: Takes the position of an [Akashic Record](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#greatwork/akashiclib), as well as a Pattern as a key, and retrieves the iota at that key from your Everbook, storing it in the given [Akashic Record](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#greatwork/akashiclib) if able.

hexal:everbook/write.d: Takes the position of an [Akashic Record](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#greatwork/akashiclib), as well as a Pattern as a key, and stores the iota in that record at that key to your Everbook at the same key.

hexal:everbook/delete.d: Takes a pattern and removes the entry with that pattern key from your Everbook.

hexal:everbook/toggle_macro.d: Takes a pattern and marks that entry of your Everbook as a Pattern that when drawn by your hand will be treated as any other of Nature's patterns.

hexal:smelt.d: Remove a location, item entity, or mote from the stack, then either smelt the block at the location or smelt all the items in the item entity or mote.

hexal:freeze.d: Freezes the block at a block location. For example, turns water into ice, and ice into packed ice. Costs one [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hexal:falling_block.d: Remove a location from the stack, and force the block there to fall as if it were sand or gravel. Costs one and a half [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hexal:place_type.d: Accepts an item type or mote and a location, and attempts to place a block of that item type at that location. If a mote was passed it will instead place from the record referenced by that mote. Costs an eighth of an [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hexal:particles.d: Accepts a location or a list of locations, and either creates a particle at the location, or creates lines of particles between the locations in the list. Costs two thousandths of an [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst) per location.

hexal:wisp/summon/projectile.d: This wisp is summoned and launched like an arrow, casting its hex on whatever it hits. The initial stack when it executes will be a reference to itself, then a reference to what it hit.

hexal:wisp/summon/ticking.d: Similar to Summon Projectile Wisp, but with only one vector input for the position to summon the wisp. Cyclic wisps are unmoving once summoned, instead executing their hex up to 20 times each second.

hexal:wisp/self.d: Add a reference to the casting wisp to the stack. This must be cast by a wisp; trying to cast it through a staff will fail rather spectacularly.

hexal:wisp/media.d: Add the amount of media in the wisp's reservoir to the stack. This must be cast by a wisp; trying to cast it through a staff will fail rather spectacularly.

hexal:wisp/hex.d: Removes a reference to a wisp from the stack, and replaces it with the wisp's contained hex. Must be a wisp you summoned, or a wisp that has [allowed](https://hexal.hexxy.media/v/0.3.1/1.0/en_us#patterns/spells/wisps@hexal:wisp/transfer/allow) transfer with the caster or caster's owner.

hexal:wisp/owner.d: Removes a reference to a wisp and an entity from the stack, and returns true if that entity owns that wisp, and false otherwise.

hexal:wisp/move/target/set.d: Removes a position vector from the stack; The Cyclic Wisp that executed this pattern will move in a straight line towards that position (colliding with terrain in its path) until it reaches it.

hexal:wisp/move/target/get.d: Adds to the stack the position vector that the executing Cyclic Wisp is currently moving towards.

hexal:wisp/move/speed/set.d: Removes a number from the stack, and sets the executing Cyclic Wisp's maximum speed to that number.

hexal:wisp/move/speed/get.d: Gets the executing Cyclic Wisp's current maximum speed.

hexal:wisp/transfer/allow.d: When two wisps are [linked](https://hexal.hexxy.media/v/0.3.1/1.0/en_us#patterns/spells/links) together, they transfer media between each other until they are balanced. By default this only happens between wisps with the same owner. This takes an index, and explicitly allows the wisp to exchange media with the linkable at that index.

hexal:wisp/transfer/disallow.d: Correspondingly, this takes an index and disallows the wisp from exchanging media with the linkable at that index.

hexal:wisp/transfer/others/allow.d: This takes a wisp that you own and an index, and allows the wisp to exchange media with the linkable at that index.

hexal:wisp/transfer/others/disallow.d: This takes a wisp that you own and an index, and disallows the wisp from exchanging media with the linkable at that index.

hexal:get_entity/wisp.d: Transform the position on the stack into the wisp at that location (or [Null](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#casting/101) if there isn't one).

hexal:zone_entity/wisp.d: Take a position and maximum distance on the stack, and combine them into a list of wisps near the position.

hexal:zone_entity/not_wisp.d: Take a position and maximum distance on the stack, and combine them into a list of non-wisp entities near the position.

hexal:wisp/trigger/tick.d: Removes an integer from the stack, then delays the wisp's next cast until at least that many twentieth's of a second have passed. This and other triggers like it will halve the wisp's upkeep cost while it isn't casting.

hexal:wisp/trigger/comm.d: The wisp's next cast will not occur until it has received at least one [communication](https://hexal.hexxy.media/v/0.3.1/1.0/en_us#patterns/spells/links@hexal:link/comm/send).

hexal:wisp/trigger/move.d: The wisp's next cast will not occur until it has reached the position it is [navigating](https://hexal.hexxy.media/v/0.3.1/1.0/en_us#patterns/spells/wisps@hexal:wisp/move/target/set) towards.

hexal:wisp/seon/get.d: Returns my currently bound wisp. A new wisp can only be bound when this returns null. (This is not a great spell, I have simply placed it here for convenience.)

hexal:link.d: Links the caster to the entity removed from the stack, which must be linkable. This costs one [Amethyst Shard](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hexal:link/others.d: May be evaluated by any casting instrument. Links two entities, which must be linkable. This costs one [Amethyst Shard](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hexal:link/unlink.d: Removes the link at the given index from the caster's links. This costs two [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hexal:link/unlink/others.d: Takes two linkables and unlinks them if they are linked. This costs two [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hexal:link/get.d: Removes an index from the stack, and adds the entity connected to the link at that index to the stack.

hexal:link/get_index.d: Removes an entity from the stack, and adds the index to the link to that entity to the stack (or -1 if the caster isn't linked to that entity).

hexal:link/num.d: Adds the number of links to the wisp to the stack.

hexal:link/comm/send.d: Removes an iota from the stack, then removes an index from the stack and sends the iota along the link at the given index.  This costs one hundredth of an [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hexal:link/comm/read.d: When something receives an iota along a link it is added to a queue. This pattern adds the first iota in the queue to the stack, removing it from the queue.

hexal:link/comm/num.d: Adds to the stack the number of unread iota in the caster's received iota queue.

hexal:link/comm/clear.d: Removes all unread iota from the caster's received iota queue.

hexal:link/comm/open_transmit.d: Similar to [Introspection](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/patterns_as_iotas@hexcasting:open_paren), until drawing a [Close Transmit](https://hexal.hexxy.media/v/0.3.1/1.0/en_us#patterns/spells/links@hexal:link/comm/close_transmit) all patterns I draw are sent along the link whose index is at the top of the stack.

hexal:link/comm/close_transmit.d: When drawn after [Open Transmit](https://hexal.hexxy.media/v/0.3.1/1.0/en_us#patterns/spells/links@hexal:link/comm/open_transmit) I stop transmitting drawn patterns. If either [Open Transmit](https://hexal.hexxy.media/v/0.3.1/1.0/en_us#patterns/spells/links@hexal:link/comm/open_transmit) or [Close Transmit](https://hexal.hexxy.media/v/0.3.1/1.0/en_us#patterns/spells/links@hexal:link/comm/close_transmit) are executed by an intermediary caster such as a wisp, they will mishap.

hexal:gate/mark.d: Consumes a gate iota and an entity. Marks that entity to be teleported the next time that gate is closed. Costs one twentieth of an [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hexal:gate/unmark.d: Consumes a gate iota and an entity. Unmarks that entity so that if it was marked with [ Gate's Opening](https://hexal.hexxy.media/v/0.3.1/1.0/en_us#patterns/great_spells/gates@hexal:gate/mark) it will no longer be teleported the next time that gate is closed.

hexal:gate/mark/get.d: Consumes a gate iota and an entity, returns whether that entity is marked by that gate.

hexal:gate/close.d: Consumes a non-drifing gate iota, or a drifting gate iota and a position. Transports all the entities marked with the passed gate to the stored or given position, as relevant. Costs half an [Amethyst Shard](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst), plus an [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst) per metre transported per entity, if the gate was drifting.

hexal:mote/storage/bind.d: Target a Mote Nexus block in the world and bind yourself to it, meaning all items you mediafy will be added to that nexus' capacity. Targeting any other block will unbind you from your currently bound nexus. Costs 32 [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hexal:mote/storage/bind/temp.d: Target a Mote Nexus block in the world and bind to it for the remainder of this cast, temporarily overriding your primary binding. Costs one thousandth of an [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hexal:mote/contained_type/get.d: Gets all the types of motes contained in the currently bound Mote Nexus.

hexal:mote/contained/get.d: Gets all the mote records from the currently bound Mote Nexus that match the passed item type or could be combined with the passed mote.

hexal:mote/storage/remaining_capacity/ge.d: Gets the remaining capacity of the bound Mote Nexus.

hexal:mote/storage/contains.d: Returns true if the Mote Nexus at the given position contains a mote of the given type, or that would stack with the given mote, and false otherwise.

hexal:mote/make.d: Convert an item in the world (either an item entity or an item frame) into a mote on your stack. If passed an existing mote instead adds the items from the entity to the mote. Mediafying an item costs a tenth of an [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hexal:mote/return.d: Returns all the items from a mote to the world at the location of your choosing. If passed a number returns at most that many items. Costs a tenth of an [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hexal:mote/combinable.d: Returns true if the first mote can be combined with the items in the second argument (which can be a mote, item stack, item entity, or item frame), and false otherwise.

hexal:mote/split.d: Splits the specified number of items off of the passed mote, creating a new mote pointing to a new mote record.

hexal:mote/storage/get.d: Get the position of the Mote Nexus that contains the passed mote.

hexal:mote/storage/set.d: Move the record referenced by the passed mote to the Mote Nexus at the passed position. This returns a new mote pointing to that record, and invalidates all previous motes pointing to that record.

hexal:mote/craft.d: Takes a mote, list of motes, or list of list of motes. returns a list containing the results of crafting with those items. For example, the input Stone x128 would return [Stone Button x128].

hexal:mote/craft/preview.d: Takes the same input as [Craft](https://hexal.hexxy.media/v/0.3.1/1.0/en_us#patterns/spells/motes@hexal:mote/craft), except it can take Item Stack Iotas as well as motes. Returns a list of Item Stack Iotas representing what the results of [Craft](https://hexal.hexxy.media/v/0.3.1/1.0/en_us#patterns/spells/motes@hexal:mote/craft) would have been with motes containing those inputs.

hexal:mote/villager/level/get.d: Accepts a villager, returns a number representing that villager's seniority and skill at their craft.

hexal:mote/trade/get.d: Accepts a villager and returns all of the trades that villager is offering. This is a list of lists of lists. Each trade comprises two lists, the cost, and the returned items. The returned items is a list containing the type of item, and the number of items.

hexal:mote/trade.d: Accepts a villager, a list of motes to trade with to villager, and optionally an int for which of that villager's trades to attempt. (int? above means that you can pass 2 or 3 arguments, the optional 3rd being an int).

hexal:mote/use_on.d: Accepts a mote, and either an entity, or a target block and a normal vector. Uses the item on the entity/block. The mote must either only have one item in it, or the items contained must be extremely simple (no NBT data).

hexal:interop/fabric_only/phase_block.d: Takes a position and a number, and phases the block at that position out for that many seconds. Costs one ten-thousandth of an [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst) times the square of the time to phase out for.

hexcassettes:enqueue.d: Enqueues a Hex to cast after that many twentieths of a second. It takes an iota to use as the label for the cassette.

hexcassettes:dequeue.d: I can also automate killing cassettes with this pattern. It takes an iota and dequeues the cassette with that label if it exists.

hexcassettes:killall.d: Terminates all cassettes, similar to the effects of the Parallel Processing mishap.

hexcassettes:specs.d: Pushes the total number of cassettes slots that I currently have.

hexcassettes:free.d: Pushes the number of non-busy cassette slots that I currently have.

hexcassettes:inspect.d: Pushes null if I do not have an active cassette with that label, or the cassette's Hex if I do. I hear rumors of this being used for iota storage and passing information between Hexes.

hexcassettes:foretell.d: Pushes null if I do not have an active cassette with that label, or how many twentieths of a second until that cassette fires if I do.

hexcellular:create_property.d: Creates a property iota for a random Property. Costs about five [Charged Amethyst](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst) to etch this law into the universe.

hexcellular:observe_property.d: Observes the current value of the property iota.

hexcellular:set_property.d: Sets the property iota. Costs about a tenth of an [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hexcellular:readonly_property.d: Creates a read-only property iota that refers to the same Property as the given property iota.

hexchanting:imbue_equipment.d: Imbues the supplied hexes into the [Amethyst](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst) equipment in my other hand, so that they will be cast whenever the item is used. Costs 9 [Charged Amethyst](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst) except on arrows, which cost 5 [Shards](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hexic:collar.d: Ties the mediaweave I am currently wearing. Costs a shard if it succeeds, or nothing if it didn't (I am either not wearing a mediaweave, or it is already tied).

hexic:connect.d: Casts the supplied Hex between each pair of elements in the given list, and splits the list at locations that return False.

hexic:decollar.d: Unties the mediaweave I am currently wearing. Costs a shard if it succeeds, or nothing if it didn't (I am either not wearing a mediaweave, or it is not tied).

hexic:dye_offpaw.d: Imbues the item held in my offhand (e.g. a [casting item](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/hexcasting)) with the given pigment.

hexic:engine/pos.d: Returns the position of the engine casting the current Hex. If any of these patterns are used outside a casting engine, mishaps rather spectacularly.

hexic:engine/sleep.d: Sleeps for at least the given number of seconds. Nature seems to round this to the next twentieth of a second.

hexic:engine/suspend.d: Suspends the current cast, as if I walked away from the engine (or stopped the rotor).

hexic:engine/terminate.d: Destroys the current cast, as if I stopped the rotor while sneaking. Any following patterns will never be cast.

hexic:erase.d: Erases the Hex or iota contained within a dropped item or block. Costs one dust per item.

hexic:extract.d: Extracts an iota from the given list, and breaks the list apart around it. Returns all items before the iota, all items after the iota, and finally the iota itself.

hexic:get_other_caster.d: Adds the closest sentient being, excluding me, to the stack.

hexic:grep.d: Discards iotas from the given list unless they satisfy the given predicate. Using [Charon's Gambit](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/meta@hexcasting:halt) discards the current and all remaining iotas.

hexic:mkmacro.d: Etches a macro into the given item entity with the given name (optional); removes a macro if the hex (topmost argument) is null. New macros cost 5 dust; replacing/removing macros is free.

hexic:modulo.d: Similar to Modulus, but differs for negative numbers: -8 %₁ 3 = -2, but -8 %₂ 3 = 1.

hexic:murmur.d: Adds the phrase on the *tip of my tongue* to the stack, regardless of whether I intend to say it.

hexic:reveal.d: Takes a list of iotas (or a single non-iota, which is treated as a list with one element) and embeds them in my mind persistently. Displayed iotas survive all methods that would clear a normal Reveal, and can only be cleared by another casting of Greater Reveal or my untimely demise.

hexic:staffcast_factory.d: Casts the given Hex as if from my staff, using its stack, etc. The Ravenmind (and perhaps other information) is carried across the boundary.

hexic:where.d: Creates a list of the indices for which True is present. For example, [True, False, True] becomes [0, 2]. I can also mix bools and ints in the input list. | Adds each index to the list based on the value. For example, [1, 2, 3] becomes [0, 1, 1, 2, 2, 2]. Zero or negative numbers do not appear at all.

hexical:normalize_scroll.d: Restores the parchment of a scroll to an unmodified state.

hexical:age_scroll.d: Yellows the parchment of an Animated Scroll, making it bear striking semblance to some ancient scrolls I've been finding.

hexical:vanish_scroll.d: Causes the Animated Scroll to become invisible leaving only the pattern, making it appear as though the pattern were magically etched into the surface the scroll is on.

hexical:color_scroll.d: Changes the color of an Animated Scroll's ink to the color specified by the vector, with the components being 0 to 1 values of red, green, and blue respectively.

hexical:glow_scroll.d: Causes the ink of an Animated Scroll to brightly glow, regardless of lighting conditions.

hexical:write_grimoire.d: Associates a pattern to a list of patterns in the Grimoire in my offhand.

hexical:erase_grimoire.d: Erases any associations for a pattern that may exist in the Grimoire in my offhand.

hexical:index_grimoire.d: Gets a list of all patterns modified by the Grimoire in my offhand.

hexical:periwinkle.d: Fortunately, the Art of Hexcasting is a versatile one and provides the means to bring back near anything.

hexical:wish.d: Wish the genie to cast a Hex for me. Because I am *teaching* a mind rather than *etching* a [casting device](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/hexcasting), I can freely reteach the genie a new Hex any time without losing media.

hexical:recharge_lamp.d: Refuels the Lamp in my offhand by the given amount in [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst). Costs just the media I'm giving the Lamp.

hexical:get_hand_lamp_position.d: Pushes my original position when I began using the Hand Lamp.

hexical:get_hand_lamp_rotation.d: Pushes my original rotation when I began using the Hand Lamp.

hexical:get_hand_lamp_velocity.d: Pushes my original velocity when I began using the Hand Lamp.

hexical:get_hand_lamp_use_time.d: Pushes how many times the Hand Lamp has cast since I began using the Hand Lamp. I can divide by by 20 to convert to seconds.

hexical:get_hand_lamp_media.d: Pushes the remaining media of the Hand Lamp, in units of dust.

hexical:get_hand_lamp_storage.d: Requests the iota I had saved to the genie to be pushed to the top of the stack. If I had not previously saved anything, the genie pushes [Null](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#casting/101).

hexical:set_hand_lamp_storage.d: Asks the genie to remember an iota for me. Strangely, the genie seems able to bypass the Transgress Others mishap, perhaps because it requires my active concentration to use this Hand Lamp.

hexical:get_arch_lamp_position.d: Pushes my original position when the [Archgenie Lamp](https://hexical.hexxy.media/v/latest/main/en_us#lamp/arch_lamps) started casting.

hexical:get_arch_lamp_rotation.d: Pushes my original rotation when the [Archgenie Lamp](https://hexical.hexxy.media/v/latest/main/en_us#lamp/arch_lamps) started casting.

hexical:get_arch_lamp_velocity.d: Pushes my original velocity when the [Archgenie Lamp](https://hexical.hexxy.media/v/latest/main/en_us#lamp/arch_lamps) started casting.

hexical:get_arch_lamp_use_time.d: Pushes how many times the [Archgenie Lamp](https://hexical.hexxy.media/v/latest/main/en_us#lamp/arch_lamps) has cast since its activation. I can divide by by 20 to convert to seconds.

hexical:get_arch_lamp_storage.d: Can be cast by a [casting device](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/hexcasting), [Staff](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/staff), or within the [Archgenie Lamp](https://hexical.hexxy.media/v/latest/main/en_us#lamp/arch_lamps) to push the stored iota.

hexical:set_arch_lamp_storage.d: Can be cast by a [casting device](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/hexcasting), [Staff](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/staff), or within the [Archgenie Lamp](https://hexical.hexxy.media/v/latest/main/en_us#lamp/arch_lamps) to remember an iota. Unlike Hand Lamp, this is subject to Transgress Others mishap.

hexical:get_arch_lamp_media.d: Pushes the remaining amount of media left in the [Archgenie Lamp](https://hexical.hexxy.media/v/latest/main/en_us#lamp/arch_lamps), in units of dust.

hexical:has_arch_lamp.d: Pushes whether a player currently has an active [Archgenie Lamp](https://hexical.hexxy.media/v/latest/main/en_us#lamp/arch_lamps).

hexical:lamp_finale.d: The instant I let go of my Hand Lamp, it casts an additional time. I can use this pattern to recognize whether a cast is that finale, and react accordingly.

hexical:rotate_block.d: Rotates a block to face a certain vector direction. Requires a rotatable block. Costs about an eighth of an [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hexical:rotate_entity.d: Rotates an entity by a given change in pitch and yaw, expressed in radians.

hexical:shuffle_pattern.d: Uses the number to shuffle the pattern into one of the same shape, but different stroke order. My notes hint that ancient Hexcasters used this for some *grand library*.

hexical:congruent.d: Pushes whether two patterns have the same shape, stroke order, and orientation.

hexical:similar.d: Pushes whether two patterns have same shape but not necessarily the same stroke order.

hexical:serialize_pattern.d: Turns a pattern into a list of numbers for my splitting, analysis, and dissection. The inverse of [Calligrapher's Purification](https://hexical.hexxy.media/v/latest/main/en_us#patterns/pattern_manipulation@hexical:deserialize_pattern).

hexical:deserialize_pattern.d: Turns a list of numbers into a pattern for my viewing and execution. The inverse of [Chirographer's Purification](https://hexical.hexxy.media/v/latest/main/en_us#patterns/pattern_manipulation@hexical:serialize_pattern).

hexical:draw_pattern.d: Takes a pattern and produces a normalized list of vectors. The z-component of these vectors is zero. I feel this may be useful for artistic Hexes.

hexical:grok_pull.d: Pushes two lists; one of the stack and one of the unfinished list building after an unclosed [Introspection](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/patterns_as_iotas@hexcasting:open_paren). Entity references to players that are not me become [Null](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#casting/101).

hexical:grok_push.d: Takes two lists of iotas and sets them as my stack and my parenthesized list respectively. Entity references to players that are not me become [Null](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#casting/101).

hexical:get_telepathy.d: By focusing on a particular image, I can detect that concentration via this pattern. Pushes how many twentieths of a second I've been intending to Call Telepathy, or -1 if I am not.

hexical:send_telepathy.d: Momentarily displays an iota above my hotbar. If cast repeatedly, each cast overwrites the previous instantly.

hexical:shout_telepathy.d: Grandly flashes an iota across my vision. It obstructs my vision and takes some time to fade in, so I shall only use it sparingly.

hexical:pling.d: Causes me to hear a pling that is inaudible to others.

hexical:click.d: Causes me to hear a click that is inaudible to others.

hexical:left_click.d: Pushes how many twentieths of a second I've been intending to Attack/Destroy, or -1 if I am not.

hexical:right_click.d: Pushes how many twentieths of a second I've been intending to Use Item/Place Block, or -1 if I am not.

hexical:moving_up.d: Pushes how many twentieths of a second I've been intending to Walk Forwards, or -1 if I am not.

hexical:moving_down.d: Pushes how many twentieths of a second I've been intending to Walk Backwards, or -1 if I am not.

hexical:moving_left.d: Pushes how many twentieths of a second I've been intending to Strafe Left, or -1 if I am not. Can be differentiated from Evade Reflection because d comes to the left of e.

hexical:moving_right.d: Pushes how many twentieths of a second I've been intending to Strafe Right, or -1 if I am not. Can be differentiated from Dodge Reflection because e comes to the right of d.

hexical:jumping.d: Pushes how many twentieths of a second I've been intending to Jump, or -1 if I am not.

hexical:sneaking.d: Pushes how many twentieths of a second I've been intending to Sneak, or -1 if I am not.

hexical:scroll.d: Pushes the change in scrolling I have performed since I have invoked Telepathy.

hexical:key_shelf.d: Reads the pattern key of an [Akashic Bookshelf](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#greatwork/akashiclib).

hexical:write_shelf.d: Writes an iota under a pattern key to an [Akashic Bookshelf](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#greatwork/akashiclib).

hexical:conjure_mage_block.d:
Conjures a Mage Blocks at the location. Costs about three [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).
*I can create a city out of nothing, or I can cover it in volcanic rock.*

hexical:reset_mage_block.d:
Conjures a Mage Blocks at the location. Costs about three [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).
*I can create a city out of nothing, or I can cover it in volcanic rock.*

hexical:modify_block_bouncy.d: Makes the block bouncy, like a Slime Block. Bounces me regardless of whether I am sneaking. Delightfully fun!

hexical:modify_block_ephemeral.d: Sets the duration after which a Mage Block will spontaneously disappear.

hexical:modify_block_energized.d: Sets the Redstone power outputted by this Mage Block.

hexical:modify_block_volatile.d: Breaking volatile Mage Blocks shatters others it is touching. This can cascade until every connected volatile block shatters.

hexical:autograph.d: Autographs the item in my offhand with my name and [Pigment](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/pigments). Autographing an item with my name already on it moves my name to the top of the list.

hexical:unautograph.d: A more destructive form of [Erase Item](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/spells/hexcasting@hexcasting:erase), capable of burning off autographs. Costs about one [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst) similar to [Erase Item](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/spells/hexcasting@hexcasting:erase).

hexical:has_autograph.d: Pushes whether a given player has signed a given item stack.

hexical:get_dye.d: Gets the dye of a block, entity, or block/item identifier.

hexical:dye.d: Dyes a dyeable block or entity. Costs about an eighth of one [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hexical:translate_dye.d: Translates a dye color into a vector, where each component is from 0 to 1 and represents the red, green, and blueness of the dye respectively.

hexical:magic_missile.d: Conjures a small silver of amethyst that always deals a full heart of damage and forces the target backwards. Costs about one [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hexical:to_pigment.d: Takes a colored dye iota and transforms it into a pigment, takes a player and returns their pigment, or takes an item containing a pigment and returns its pigment.

hexical:sample_pigment.d: Samples the pigment at a certain place and time as a vector, where each component is from 0 to 1 and represents the red, green, and blueness respectively.

hexical:prestidigitation.d: Causes a small magical effect, not too distinct from the original nature or function of the target. Costs about a tenth of one [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hexical:wristpocket.d: This spell vanishes the stack of items in my other hand, or conjures it back, swapping if my other hand is holding something. Costs about a eighth of one [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hexical:wristpocket_item.d: Returns the item in my wristpocket, or [Null](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#casting/101) if it is empty.

hexical:sleight.d: Performs an act of magical sleight of hand to steal items into my wristpocket or expel my wristpocket back into the world. Costs about a fourth of one [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hexical:mage_hand.d: Projects my mind's hand forward to use my wristpocketed item and interact with the world. If my wristpocket is empty, acts as though a plain hand had reached out. Costs about one [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hexical:mage_mouth.d: Makes me eat my wristpocketed item, nourishing me or applying potions to me. Costs about one [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst) and mishaps if the item is not edible.

hexical:conjure_speck.d: Conjures a speck with the iota, position, and rotation. Costs a negligible amount of media. Pushes the speck iota to the stack.

hexical:move_specklike.d: Moves a speck entity to the position.

hexical:rotate_specklike.d: Rotates a speck entity to face the vector.

hexical:roll_specklike.d: Accepts a number between 0 and 1, representing a fraction of a full rotation, and rotates the speck's image by that amount.

hexical:size_specklike.d: Scales the speck, can range from 0 to 10. Represents size in blocks and is zero by default.

hexical:thickness_specklike.d: Changes the stroke thickness of a pattern speck, can range from 0 to 10. Represents twentieths of a block, and is zero by default.

hexical:lifetime_specklike.d: Commands the speck to disappear after that many twentieths of a second.

hexical:pigment_specklike.d: Splashes a pigment iota onto the speck, changing its color after creation.

hexical:zone_specklike.d: Returns specks similarly to other [zone distillation](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/entities@hexcasting:zone_entity/animal) patterns.

hexical:egg.d: Conjures an egg. May be fertile. Costs about two [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hexical:llama_spit.d: Conjures a sticky low-damaging projectile. Costs about a fourth of one [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hexical:snowball.d: Conjures a harmless snowball. Costs about half of an [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hexical:ghast_fireball.d: Conjures an explosive fireball that can be *percussively propelled*. Costs about three [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hexical:confetti.d: Creates a loud bang similar to that of [Fireworks](https://hexical.hexxy.media/v/latest/main/en_us#patterns/spells/pyrotechnics) and a burst of colorful particles, either in a direction or in a radial blast. Costs about half of one [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hexical:vibration.d: Causes a visible pulse of vibration from a vector to an entity or vector over a number of seconds. Costs about a sixteenth of one [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hexical:sparkle.d: Produces a small sparkling particle of my desired position, color, and lifespan. Costs a negligible amount of media.

hexical:jailbreak.d: Cracks the unprogrammed [casting device](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/hexcasting) or [Curio](https://hexical.hexxy.media/v/latest/main/en_us#items/curios) in my offhand. Cracked casting devices proudly display their Hexes. Costs about one [Charged Amethyst](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hexical:flower.d: Conjures a flower of my choosing at a location. I must have identified this flower at some point before. Costs about a quarter of an [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hexical:light.d: Conjures a completely invisible light with illumination strength of my choosing at a location. Costs about a quarter of an [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hexical:gasp.d: Instantly replenishes a creature's air bubbles. Costs about one [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hexical:parrot.d: Emits a sound associated with a mob near a location, as though a parrot had imitated that mob. Costs about a half of an [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hexical:break_fortune.d: Targets structural faults in a block, resulting in a higher yield. Costs about one, three, and five [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst) when power input is 0, 1, and 2 respectively.

hexical:break_silk.d: Breaks a block gently, perserving the block better than standard mining. Costs about half of an [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hexical:conjure_gummy.d: Conjures a Hex Gummy: a delightful light snack that also provides about a tenth of an [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst)'s worth of media. Costs about one [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hexical:conjure_hexburst.d: Conjures a Hexburst of the given iota at the location. Costs about one [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst) and is subject to the Transgress Others mishap.

hexical:conjure_hextito.d: Conjures a Hextito of the given Hex at the location. Costs about two [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst) and is subject to the Transgress Others mishap.

hexical:spike.d: Takes a non-air position, an axis vector, and a delay in seconds up to ten seconds long and conjures a spike at that location. Costs about one [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hexical:piston.d: Takes a block position and an axis vector and pushes the block along that vector. Costs an eighth of an [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hexical:dispense.d: Takes an item entity, a position, and an axis vector and dispenses the item. For most applications, costs about half of one [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hexical:smelt.d: Takes an item entity and cooks it as if in a Furnace. Costs about one [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst) for every ten seconds that the Furnace would need to have been active.

hexical:roast.d: A specialized variant of [Cook](https://hexical.hexxy.media/v/latest/main/en_us#patterns/spells/block_mimicry@hexical:smelt) that simulates a Campfire instead. This has a much more limited set of possibilities; I am unsure why I would ever use this.

hexical:smoke.d: A specialized variant of [Cook](https://hexical.hexxy.media/v/latest/main/en_us#patterns/spells/block_mimicry@hexical:smelt) that simulates a Smoker instead, making it unable to process anything but foods but at a faster rate, making the spell cheaper.

hexical:blast.d: A specialized variant of [Cook](https://hexical.hexxy.media/v/latest/main/en_us#patterns/spells/block_mimicry@hexical:smelt) that simulates a Blast Furnace instead, making it unable to process anything but ores but at a faster rate, making the spell cheaper.

hexical:stonecut.d: Takes an item entity and cuts the item into the shape of an item identifier. Costs about an eighth of one [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hexical:displace.d: Teleports an entity within the [circle](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#greatwork/spellcircles) to another point within the same [circle](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#greatwork/spellcircles). Unlike [Greater Teleport](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/great_spells/teleport), this spell takes in world coordinates rather than an offset. Costs about half of an [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hexical:absorb_arm.d: Allows a [circle](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#greatwork/spellcircles) to hook onto a [Pedestal](https://hexical.hexxy.media/v/latest/main/en_us#items/pedestals) within ambit to use as its *other arm*. Useful for certain spells that demand an item held in my other hand. It also works as a [Wristpocket](https://hexical.hexxy.media/v/latest/main/en_us#patterns/spells/wristpocket).

hexical:create_dust.d: Exports media out of an [Impetus](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#greatwork/impetus) at a rate of about eleven [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst) spent per ten [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst) created. Takes a location and a number of up to a stack of [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hexical:get_evocation.d: Pushes the Hex etched into my mind.

hexical:set_evocation.d:
Etches a Hex, allowing me to cast it by holding Evoke for one second. Costs about one [Charged Amethyst](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).
*Anthony thought at it, and it turned a flip-flop on the grass, and lay trembling, its eyes gleaming in small black terror.*

hexical:is_evoking.d: Pushes how long since a player has been evoking. Is -1 if they are not currently evoking.

hexical:conjure_firework.d: Conjures a firework of my *exact* specifications. It may be one of the most complex spells in existence. Costs equivalently to the other firework spell.
hexical:conjure_firework.i: vec, vec, num, num, list of vec, list of vec, bool, bool

hexical:simulate_firework.d: Analyzes the Firework Star in my other hand and conjures a firework of that star, with the position, velocity, and gunpowder amount specified. Costs about one [Amethyst Shard](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hexical:get_hotbar.d: Pushes a number relating to which of my current items I am currently holding.

hexical:set_hotbar.d:
Takes a number 0 to 8 and switches my current item to it.
*Remember, switching to your pistol is always faster than reloading.*

hexical:set_lesser_sentinels.d: Dismisses any existing Lesser Sentinels and deploys a Lesser Sentinel at every position in the list.

hexical:get_lesser_sentinels.d: Returns a list of vectors corresponding to the positions of all my Lesser Sentinels.

hexical:item_name.d: Takes an item and renames it to the text given. Resets name if given [Null](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#casting/101). Free.

hexical:item_lore.d: Takes an item and a list of text to append as a description. Clears if given [Null](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#casting/101). Free.

hexical:shader_clear.d: Breaks any shader spell currently applied to me. Useful for "bleaching" my eyes after too much experimentation.

hexical:shader_owl.d: Greatly augments my ability to see in the dark, although the light resultingly becomes extremely blinding.

hexical:shader_lines.d: Transforms the world into a thin outline of black and white. Possibly useful for identifying subtle contrasts.

hexical:shader_tv.d: Alters my vision to contain strange lines and make objects towards the center of my vision bulge "towards" me. Seems to be in reference to something...

hexical:shader_media.d: Transforms my vision to perceive only the most important things...

hexical:shader_spider.d: Splits my vision into multiple sections, similar to what a spider might see. I am unsure whether it actually grants me more vision...

hexical:hopper.d: Instantly transports all items from source to destination. Cost scales based on the amount of mass transferred - a stack of 64 items will cost about three [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst). Numbers are optional; details later.

hexical:index_hopper.d: Applies to sources that support slots; inventories. Returns a list of the item stacks contained within them, with their index in the list being their slot number.

hexical:horrible.d: Judging by the pattern signature, I can only imagine that it summons something.

hexical:write_charmed.d: Writes an iota to the charmed item’s internal storage. Subject to the Transgress Others mishap.

hexical:read_charmed.d: Pushes the stored iota from the charmed item’s internal storage.

hexical:write_charmed_proxy.d: If the item charged features an iota storage by default, such as a [Focus](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/focus), writes an iota into it.

hexical:read_charmed_proxy.d: If the item charged features an iota storage by default, such as a [Focus](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/focus), reads an iota from it.

hexical:discharm.d: Removes a charm from an item without affecting any other property. Costs about one [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hexical:weave_mesh.d: Takes a list of vectors, with constraints defined on the prior page, and weaves the mesh into that shape. Free.

hexical:read_mesh.d: Pushes the shape of a mesh as a list of vectors.

hexodus:alter_ballast.d: Commands a Ballast on my person to fall in a given direction with a given strength strength. Free.

hexodus:change_gravity.d: Takes an entity, an axial vector for new gravity, and a strength scalar relative to standard pull. Specifics are detailed on the next page. | Takes a Ship, an axial vector for new gravity, and a strength scalar relative to standard pull. Costs one dust per kg of mass.
hexodus:change_gravity.i: entity, vector, number | ship, axis_angle, num

hexodus:get_duration.d: Pushes the remaining twentieths of a second that [Gravitate](https://miyucomics.github.io/hexodus/v/1.0.0/1.0.0/en_us#patterns/spells/gravity@hexodus:change_gravity) will affect an entity. Zero if the entity is not under the effects of [Gravitate](https://miyucomics.github.io/hexodus/v/1.0.0/1.0.0/en_us#patterns/spells/gravity@hexodus:change_gravity). | Pushes the remaining twentieths of a second that [Gravitate](https://techtastic.github.io/HexxySkies/v/latest/master/en_us#interop/hexodus_navimancy@hexodus:change_gravity) will affect a Ship. Zero if the Ship is not under the effects of [Gravitate](https://techtastic.github.io/HexxySkies/v/latest/master/en_us#interop/hexodus_navimancy@hexodus:change_gravity).

hexodus:get_direction.d: Pushes the direction that [Gravitate](https://miyucomics.github.io/hexodus/v/1.0.0/1.0.0/en_us#patterns/spells/gravity@hexodus:change_gravity) is attempting to drag an entity, or [Null](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#casting/101) if the entity is not under the effects of [Gravitate](https://miyucomics.github.io/hexodus/v/1.0.0/1.0.0/en_us#patterns/spells/gravity@hexodus:change_gravity). | Pushes the direction that [Gravitate](https://techtastic.github.io/HexxySkies/v/latest/master/en_us#interop/hexodus_navimancy@hexodus:change_gravity) is attempting to drag a Ship, or [Null](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#casting/101) if the Ship is not under the effects of [Gravitate](https://techtastic.github.io/HexxySkies/v/latest/master/en_us#interop/hexodus_navimancy@hexodus:change_gravity).

hexodus:get_strength.d: Pushes the scaling factor of [Gravitate](https://miyucomics.github.io/hexodus/v/1.0.0/1.0.0/en_us#patterns/spells/gravity@hexodus:change_gravity)'s gravity compared to baseline, or [Null](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#casting/101) if the entity is not under the effects of [Gravitate](https://miyucomics.github.io/hexodus/v/1.0.0/1.0.0/en_us#patterns/spells/gravity@hexodus:change_gravity). | Pushes the scaling factor of [Gravitate](https://techtastic.github.io/HexxySkies/v/latest/master/en_us#interop/hexodus_navimancy@hexodus:change_gravity)'s gravity compared to baseline, or [Null](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#casting/101) if the Ship is not under the effects of [Gravitate](https://techtastic.github.io/HexxySkies/v/latest/master/en_us#interop/hexodus_navimancy@hexodus:change_gravity).

hexodus:get_true_direction.d: Pushes the direction of Gravity acting on an entity. | Pushes the direction of Gravity acting on a Ship.

hexodus:get_true_strength.d: Pushes strength of Gravity acting on an entity compared to baseline. | Pushes strength of Gravity acting on a Ship compared to baseline.

hexpose:am_enlightened.d: Pushes whether the given player has achieved Enlightenment.

hexpose:is_brainswept.d: Pushes whether an entity has been "magically relieved of its mind". I feel this is strongly related to [Flay Mind](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/great_spells/brainsweep) somehow...

hexpose:create_text.d: Takes an iota and returns a [text iota](https://miyucomics.github.io/hexpose/v/1.0.0/1.0.0/en_us#patterns/text_iotas) representing it. If taking a [text iota](https://miyucomics.github.io/hexpose/v/1.0.0/1.0.0/en_us#patterns/text_iotas), strips all the styles of it.

hexpose:split_text.d: Splits a [text iota](https://miyucomics.github.io/hexpose/v/1.0.0/1.0.0/en_us#patterns/text_iotas) into a list of individual glyphs.

hexpose:combine_text.d: Transforms all the elements of a list into text (or keeps them if they were) and pastes it all together.

hexpose:text_color.d: Takes a [text iota](https://miyucomics.github.io/hexpose/v/1.0.0/1.0.0/en_us#patterns/text_iotas) and a color encoded as a vector whose components range from 0 to 1, and produces a [text iota](https://miyucomics.github.io/hexpose/v/1.0.0/1.0.0/en_us#patterns/text_iotas) of that color.

hexpose:text_bold.d: Takes a [text iota](https://miyucomics.github.io/hexpose/v/1.0.0/1.0.0/en_us#patterns/text_iotas) and sets whether it is **bold**.

hexpose:text_italics.d: Takes a [text iota](https://miyucomics.github.io/hexpose/v/1.0.0/1.0.0/en_us#patterns/text_iotas) and sets whether it is in *italics*.

hexpose:text_underline.d: Takes a [text iota](https://miyucomics.github.io/hexpose/v/1.0.0/1.0.0/en_us#patterns/text_iotas) and sets whether it is __underlined__.

hexpose:text_strikethrough.d: Takes a [text iota](https://miyucomics.github.io/hexpose/v/1.0.0/1.0.0/en_us#patterns/text_iotas) and sets whether it has been ~~struck through~~.

hexpose:text_obfuscated.d: Takes a [text iota](https://miyucomics.github.io/hexpose/v/1.0.0/1.0.0/en_us#patterns/text_iotas) and sets whether it is obfusca||ted||.

hexpose:fluid_raycast.d: Works similar to [Archer's Distillation](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/basics@hexcasting:raycast) but targets only liquids, piercing through all other blocks.

hexpose:fluid_surface_raycast.d: Works similar to [Architect's Distillation](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/basics@hexcasting:raycast/axis) but targets only liquids, piercing through all other blocks.

hexpose:piercing_raycast.d: Works similar to [Archer's Distillation](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/basics@hexcasting:raycast) but accepts an additional identifier. It will pierce all blocks until it hits the block specified by the identifier.

hexpose:piercing_surface_raycast.d: Works similar to [Architect's Distillation](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/basics@hexcasting:raycast/axis) but accepts an additional identifier. It will pierce all blocks until it hits the block specified by the identifier.

hexpose:block_hardness.d: Pushes how difficult blocks of this type are to mine.

hexpose:block_blast_resistance.d: Pushes how resistant blocks of this type are to explosions.

hexpose:blockstate_rotation.d: Pushes the vector of the block's facing direction, or [Null](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#casting/101) if blocks of its type do not have an orientation.

hexpose:blockstate_crop.d: Pushes a number 0 to 1 corresponding to the growth progress of that block. Works for crops, Beehives, Composters, Cauldrons, and strangely Cakes too.

hexpose:get_blockstates.d: Pushes a list of all facets of that block.

hexpose:query_blockstate.d: Takes a block and a facet and pushes that facet's value.

hexpose:block_map_color.d: Pushes the color blocks of this type appear as on a map.

hexpose:get_chat.d: Applies [News Reflection](https://miyucomics.github.io/hexpose/v/1.0.0/1.0.0/en_us#patterns/scrying/chat@hexpose:get_message) to the last up to 32 messages in chat, wraps each in a list, and pushes a list of those lists.

hexpose:get_message.d: Pushes a [text iota](https://miyucomics.github.io/hexpose/v/1.0.0/1.0.0/en_us#patterns/text_iotas) of the last person to use chat, a [text iota](https://miyucomics.github.io/hexpose/v/1.0.0/1.0.0/en_us#patterns/text_iotas) of the message, and a number of twenieths of a second since that message sent.

hexpose:get_enchantments.d: Gets a list of enchantments the item has.

hexpose:get_enchantment_strength.d: Gets the strength of the specific enchantment on the item.

hexpose:entity_width.d: Similar to [Stadiometer's Purification](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/basics@hexcasting:get_entity_height) but pushes the width of an entity rather than its height.

hexpose:theodolite.d: Similar to [Alidade's Purification](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/basics@hexcasting:get_entity_look) but pushes the vector that points upwards from their head rather than the entity's facing vector.

hexpose:get_health.d: Pushes how close an entity is to death. I can think of these in terms of half-hearts.

hexpose:get_max_health.d: Pushes how much health an entity can have at its prime. I can think of these in terms of half-hearts.

hexpose:burning.d: Pushes the number of seconds the burning entity will continue burning if not put out. -1 if the entity is not burning currently.

hexpose:is_wet.d: Pushes whether the entity is touching rain, water, or in a bubble column.

hexpose:get_air.d: Pushes the number of seconds before an entity will start to suffocate. This applies to marine creatures out of water as well as land creatures in water.

hexpose:get_max_air.d: Pushes the number of seconds a regular entity of that type can last outside their normal breathing environment before they start suffocating.

hexpose:is_sleeping.d: Pushes whether the Player, Cat, Fox, or other entity is sleeping.

hexpose:is_sprinting.d: Pushes whether the Player, Cat, Fox, or other entity is sprinting. Swimming and leaving the ground after starting to sprint are still included.

hexpose:is_baby.d: Pushes whether a living creature is a baby. Also works on Armor Stands oddly.

hexpose:breedable.d: Pushes whether an animal creature is in love and ready to mate, or [Null](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#casting/101) if that creature is not capable of that type of reproduction.

hexpose:get_player_hunger.d: Pushes how full a Player is. I can think of this in terms of half-hunches.

hexpose:get_player_saturation.d: Pushes a Player's saturation, which roughly correlates to how long the Player will remain full.

hexpose:entity_vehicle.d: Pushes the entity the given entity is riding or [Null](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#casting/101) if it is not riding in or on anything.

hexpose:entity_passengers.d: Pushes a list of entities that are riding the given entity.

hexpose:shooter.d: Pushes the shooter of the given projectile entity or [Null](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#casting/101) if it has no shooter or isn't a projectile. It also pushes [Null](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#casting/101) if the shooter is outside my ambit.

hexpose:pet_owner.d: Pushes the player that has tamed this animal, or [Null](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#casting/101) if it is untamed or the player is out of ambit.

hexpose:absorption_hearts.d: Pushes the number of magical hearts this player has. I can think of these in terms of half-hearts.

hexpose:env_ambit.d: Pushes whether a location or entity is in ambit.

hexpose:env_staff.d: Pushes whether a [Staff](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/staff) is being used to cast this pattern.

hexpose:env_offhand.d: Pushes whether the dominant hand of the caster is being used to cast this pattern. May return strange results for casters without hands.

hexpose:env_packaged_hex.d: Pushes whether any form of [casting device](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/hexcasting) is being used to cast this pattern.

hexpose:env_circle.d: Pushes whether some form of [*grand work*](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#greatwork/spellcircles) is being used to cast this pattern.

hexpose:edible.d: Takes in an item identifier and pushes whether I can eat it.

hexpose:get_hunger.d: Takes in an item identifier and pushes the amount it will fill me.

hexpose:get_saturation.d: Takes in an item identifier and pushes the saturation value, which roughly affects how long it will fill me.

hexpose:is_meat.d: Takes in an item identifier and pushes whether it's considered a meat. Wolves can eat meats.

hexpose:is_snack.d: Takes in an item identifier and pushes whether it's a snack.

hexpose:identify.d: Pushes the identifier of an entity or block at a vector.

hexpose:classify.d: Pushes the identifier of an iota's type. Can be used to determine whether two iota are the same type.

hexpose:get_stack.d: Pushes the item that an Item in the world is.

hexpose:create_stack.d: Creates an item iota from an item identifier and the number of items in the stack.

hexpose:get_mainhand.d: Returns the item in the entity's mainhand.

hexpose:get_offhand.d: Returns the item in the entity's offhand.

hexpose:get_armor.d: Returns a list of all items the entity is wearing, from feet up.

hexpose:get_ender_chest.d: Returns a list of all items in my ender chest.

hexpose:get_inventory.d: Returns a list of all items the entity is carrying, or [Null](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#casting/101) if the entity can not hold items. Trying to access another Player's inventory will incur a mishap.

hexpose:get_block_inventory.d: Returns a list of all items in the container, or [Null](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#casting/101) if the block can not contain items.

hexpose:count_stack.d: Takes in an item and pushes how many items are in it.

hexpose:count_max_stack.d: Takes in an item and pushes how many items that can stack in it.

hexpose:damage_stack.d: Takes in an item and pushes how much damage the item has sustained.

hexpose:damage_max_stack.d: Takes in an item and pushes how much durability the item can have at its peak.

hexpose:item_variant.d: If this item is subceptible to [Caster's Glamour](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/spells/cyclevariant), pushes the index of the current form it's taking on. Otherwise pushes [Null](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#casting/101).

hexpose:item_variant_max.d: If this item is subceptible to [Caster's Glamour](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/spells/cyclevariant), pushes the number of forms it's capable of. Otherwise pushes [Null](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#casting/101).

hexpose:item_name.d: Gets the name given to this item.

hexpose:item_lore.d: Gets the lore written into this item.

hexpose:read_book.d: Pushes a list of [text iotas](https://miyucomics.github.io/hexpose/v/1.0.0/1.0.0/en_us#patterns/text_iotas) contained inside a book or [Null](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#casting/101) if it isn't a book.

hexpose:book_sources.d: Pushes the author of a book and its generation number.

hexpose:item_rarity.d: Gauges the rarity of an item as a number, with greater values corresponding to a rarer item. Certain aspects such as enchantments can also elevate an item's rarity.

hexpose:get_effects_entity.d: Pushes a list of status effects the entity is afflicted with.

hexpose:get_effects_item.d: Pushes a list of status effects the food or potion will bestow.

hexpose:get_effect_category.d: Pushes the general "goodness" of the effect towards the afflicted. -1 for harmful, 0 for neutral, and 1 for beneficial.

hexpose:get_effect_amplifier.d: Pushes how potent the effect type is acting on the entity or [Null](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#casting/101) if the entity doesn't have it.

hexpose:get_effect_duration.d: Pushes how long the effect type will affect the entity in twentieths of a second or [Null](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#casting/101) if the entity doesn't have it.

hexpose:villager_level.d: Pushes how advanced a villager is as a number, encoding mastery of their craft.

hexpose:villager_profession.d: Pushes the profession of a villager as an identifier

hexpose:villager_type.d: Pushes the ambient cultural aspect tied to the villager’s origin, such as desert or taiga roots.

hexpose:biome_to_villager.d: Projects the villager archetype most attuned to the essence of the specified biome, or [Null](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#casting/101) if none can be drawn.

hexpose:get_media.d: Pushes the amount of media inside an item, that a creature contains or holds, or that a specialized media-holding block contains.

hexpose:media_max_stack.d: Takes in an item and pushes either [Null](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#casting/101) if the item does not have any media-holding potential, or the amount of media it is capable of holding at its peak.

hexpose:get_weather.d: Pushes a number corresponding to the weather. 0 for clear, 1 for rain, and 2 for thundering.

hexpose:get_light.d: Pushes the light level at the position as a number 0 to 15. If inside a nontransparent block, it returns zero.

hexpose:get_power.d: Pushes the Redstone power that a position receives.

hexpose:get_comparator.d: Pushes the power level a Comparator would output if pressed against a position.

hexpose:get_day.d: Pushes the progress of the day as a number between 0 (start) and 1 (end) of the day.

hexpose:get_time.d: Pushes the twentieths of a second since the creation of the world, unaffected by events such as sleeping.

hexpose:get_moon.d: Pushes the current phase of the Moon as a fraction of its size.

hexpose:get_biome.d: Pushes the identifier of the type of biome the vector is within.

hexpose:get_dimension.d: Pushes the identifier of the dimension the Hex is being cast in.

hexpose:get_einstein.d: Pushes whether Compasses and Clocks will work in this dimension.

hexpose:cat_variant.d: Pushes the variant of the Cat.

hexpose:creeper_fuse.d: Pushes the progress of a Creeper to explosion.

hexpose:item_frame_rotation.d: Pushes the rotation of an Item Frame as an integer 0 to 7.

hexpose:painting_variant.d: Pushes the variant of the Painting.

hexssence:extract_essence.d: Extracts the essence from a dropped item. Cost varies depending on target item.

hexssence:combine_essence.d: Remove a list of vectors, a recipe iota, and a vector from the stack, then take essences from the jars at the given locations, mix them according to the given recipe, and summon the resulting item at the given location.

hexssence:decay_recipe.d:
Decays a Recipe iota into a list of lists where the inner lists each contain an item type and a count.
This list of lists represents which essences the recipe needs, and how much of each.

hextrapats:rot_about/x.d: Rotates the vector by the given angle in radians around the X axis.

hextrapats:rot_about/y.d: Rotates the vector by the given angle in radians around the Y axis.

hextrapats:rot_about/z.d: Rotates the vector by the given angle in radians around the Z axis.

hextrapats:cons_about/x.d: Converts an angle in radians to a unit vector where X=0. +Z at 0 radians and +Y at pi/4 radians.

hextrapats:cons_about/y.d: Converts an angle in radians to a unit vector where Y=0. +Z at 0 radians and -X at pi/4 radians. I've seen some texts related to this pattern mentioning something called F3, but I couldn't figure out what that means.

hextrapats:cons_about/z.d: Converts an angle in radians to a unit vector where Z=0. -X at 0 radians and +Y at pi/4 radians.

hextrapats:normalize.d: Sets the length of the vector to one.

hextrapats:len_eq.d: If the two vectors are the same length (within small tolerance), return True. Otherwise, return False.

hextrapats:len_neq.d: If the two vectors are not the same length (outside small tolerance), return True. Otherwise, return False.

hextrapats:in_range.d: If the first number is between the second and third, return True. Otherwise, return False. If the first value is a vector, compare its length instead.

hextrapats:out_range.d: If the first number is not between the second and third, return True. Otherwise, return False. If the first value is a vector, compare its length instead.

hextrapats:increment.d: Adds 1. | Increases length by 1. Does nothing if the vector is (0, 0, 0).

hextrapats:decrement.d: Subtracts by 1. | Decreases length by 1. Does nothing if the vector is (0, 0, 0).

hextrapats:approach.d: Moves the first value closer to the second by the given amount. Will not overshoot. | Moves the first vector towards the second by a given distance. Will not overshoot.
hextrapats:approach.i: num, num, num | vec, vec, num

hextrapats:angle_dist.d: Returns the shortest angular distance between two angles in radians. | Returns the shortest angular distance on a sphere between two vectors in radians

hextrapats:angle_approach.d: Turns the first angle towards the second by the given number of radians, picking whichever direction is shorter. | Rotates the first vector towards the direction of the second vector by the given number of radians. Mishaps if the two directions are directly opposite to each other.
hextrapats:angle_approach.i: num, num, num | vec, vec, num

hextrapats:set_insert_ret.d: Remove the iota at the top of the stack, then add it to the set. Return True if it wasn't already in the set, otherwise return False. The iota's type must match the set's type.

hextrapats:set_remove_ret.d: Remove the iota from top of the stack, then remove it set. Return True if it was previously in the set, otherwise return False. The iota's type must match the set's type.

hextrapats:vec/get/x.d: Returns the X, Y, or Z component of a vector.

hextrapats:vec/get/y.d: Returns the X, Y, or Z component of a vector.

hextrapats:vec/get/z.d: Returns the X, Y, or Z component of a vector.

hextrapats:vec/set/x.d: Overrides a vector's X, Y, or Z component.

hextrapats:vec/set/y.d: Overrides a vector's X, Y, or Z component.

hextrapats:vec/set/z.d: Overrides a vector's X, Y, or Z component.

hextrapats:round/int.d: Rounds a number to the nearest integer. If passed a vector, rounds each of its components instead.

hextrapats:round/exact.d: Rounds a number to the nearest multiple of the second number. If passed a vector, rounds each of its components instead.

hextrapats:deg_to_rad.d: Converts an angle in degrees to an angle in radians. Essentially multiplies by [pi](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/consts@hexcasting:const/double/pi) then divides by 180.

hextrapats:rad_to_deg.d: Converts an angle in radians to an angle in degrees. Essentially multiplies by 180 then divides by [pi](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/consts@hexcasting:const/double/pi).

hextrapats:rand_zero.d: Returns a random number between 0 (inclusive) and the number (exclusive).

hextrapats:rand_range.d: Returns a random number between the first number (inclusive) and the second (exclusive).

hextrapats:rand_vec.d: Returns a unit vector facing a random direction.

hextrapats:vec_dist.d: Returns the distance between two vectors.

hextrapats:from_polar.d: Creates a unit vector from two polar angles, pitch and yaw, in radians. +Y is up. 0 yaw is +Z, pi/2 yaw is -X. Yet again, mentions of F3 turn up.

hextrapats:to_polar.d: Converts a vector's direction into two polar angles, pitch and yaw, in radians. +Y is up. 0 yaw is +Z, pi/2 yaw is -X. Yet again, mentions of F3 turn up.

hextrapats:swap_vec_list.d: Converts a list of 3 numbers to a vector, or a vector into a list of 3 numbers.

hextrapats:haha_ha_one.d: The left-hand counter-clockwise pattern adds (1, 1, 1) to the stack; the right-hand clockwise pattern adds (-1, -1, -1).

hextrapats:eno_ah_ahah.d: The left-hand counter-clockwise pattern adds (1, 1, 1) to the stack; the right-hand clockwise pattern adds (-1, -1, -1).

hextrapats:peek/front.d: Gets the iota at the front of the list without removing it from the list.

hextrapats:peek/back.d: Gets the iota at the end of the list without removing it from the list.

hextrapats:peek/index.d: Gets the Nth iota of the list without removing it from the list. Returns [Null](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#casting/101) if the number is out of bounds.

hextrapats:split_list.d: Splits a list at the given index. [a, b, c, d, e], 2 will return [a, b], [c, d, e].

hextrapats:del_element/first.d: Remove the iota at the top of the stack, then remove the first instance of it from the list. If that iota was in the list, return True. Otherwise, return False.

hextrapats:del_element/all.d: Remove the iota at the top of the stack, then remove *all* instances of it from the list. Returns the number of removed occurrences.

hextrapats:swindle_list.d: Reorders the elements of a list the same way [Swindler's Gambit](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/stackmanip@hexcasting:swizzle) reorders the stack. Inputting a negative code will reorder the elements at the start instead of the end.

hextrapats:scronglwfijspoivjqwofklcrvewb.d: Shuffles the order of elements in the list.

hextrapats:nocon/bool_coerce.d: Convert an argument to a boolean. The number 0, Null, False, the vector (0, 0, 0), and the empty list become False; everything else becomes True.

hextrapats:nocon/greater.d: If the first argument is greater than the second, return True. Otherwise, return False.

hextrapats:nocon/less.d: If the first argument is less than the second, return True. Otherwise, return False.

hextrapats:nocon/greater_eq.d: If the first argument is greater than or equal to the second, return True. Otherwise, return False.

hextrapats:nocon/less_eq.d: If the first argument is less than or equal to the second, return True. Otherwise, return False.

hextrapats:nocon/len_eq.d: If the two vectors are the same length (within small tolerance), return True. Otherwise, return False.

hextrapats:nocon/len_neq.d: If the two vectors are not the same length (outside small tolerance), return True. Otherwise, return False.

hextrapats:nocon/eq.d: If the first argument equals the second (within a small tolerance), return True. Otherwise, return False.

hextrapats:nocon/neq.d: If the first argument does not equal the second (outside a small tolerance), return True. Otherwise, return False.

hextrapats:empty_set/num.d: Push an empty set that can hold numbers to the top of the stack.

hextrapats:empty_set/vec.d: Push an empty set that can hold vectors to the top of the stack.

hextrapats:empty_set/entity.d: Push an empty set that can hold entities to the top of the stack.

hextrapats:last_n_set.d: Remove *num* iota from the top of the stack, then add them to a set at the top of the stack. Must be either all numbers, all vectors, or all entities.

hextrapats:splat_set.d: Remove the set at the top of the stack, then push its contents to the stack. The order is up to Nature's whims.

hextrapats:set_to_list.d: Converts the set at the top of the stack to a list. The order is up to Nature's whims.

hextrapats:list_to_set.d: Converts the list at the top of the stack to a set. The list must be non-empty and entirely numbers, vectors, or entities.

hextrapats:true_eval.d: Casts a pattern or list of patterns like [Hermes' Gambit](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/meta@hexcasting:eval) if the next iota from the top of the stack is [considered True by Nature](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/logic@hexcasting:bool_coerce).

hextrapats:false_eval.d: Casts a pattern or list of patterns like [Hermes' Gambit](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/meta@hexcasting:eval) if the next iota from the top of the stack is [considered False by Nature](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/logic@hexcasting:bool_coerce).

hextrapats:true_halt.d: Forcibly halts a Hex like [Charon's Gambit](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/meta@hexcasting:halt) if the iota at the top of the stack is [considered True by Nature](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/logic@hexcasting:bool_coerce).

hextrapats:false_halt.d: Forcibly halts a Hex like [Charon's Gambit](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/meta@hexcasting:halt) if the iota at the top of the stack is [considered False by Nature](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/logic@hexcasting:bool_coerce).
