hextrapats:index_for_each.d: Casts like [Thoth's Gambit](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/meta@hexcasting:for_each), however the new stack for each element additionally has the index of that element added to the top.

hextrapats:main_for_each.d: Casts like [Thoth's Gambit](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/meta@hexcasting:for_each), however each sub-execution operates on the main stack instead of copies of the stack.

hextrapats:main_index_for_each.d: Casts like [Djehuty's Gambit](https://meepoffaith.github.io/hextra-patterns/v/1.9.1+1.20.1/1.1/en_us#patterns/hextrapats_meta@hextrapats:index_for_each), however each sub-execution operates on the main stack instead of copies of the stack.

hextrapats:nulls/coalesce.d: If the first argument is not [Null](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#casting/101), returns it. Otherwise, returns the second argument.

hextrapats:nulls/exec.d: If the first argument is not [Null](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#casting/101), returns it. Otherwise, executes the second argument, much like [Hermes' Gambit](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/meta@hexcasting:eval).

hextrapats:capsizing.d: Sends the iota on the top of the stack to the bottom of the stack.

hextrapats:capsizing/copy.d: Like [Capsizing Gambit](https://meepoffaith.github.io/hextra-patterns/v/1.9.1+1.20.1/1.1/en_us#patterns/hextrapats_stackmanip@hextrapats:capsizing), but copies the iota instead of moving it.

hextrapats:dredging.d: Pulls the iota at the bottom of the stack to the top of the stack.

hextrapats:dredging/copy.d: Like [Dredging Gambit](https://meepoffaith.github.io/hextra-patterns/v/1.9.1+1.20.1/1.1/en_us#patterns/hextrapats_stackmanip@hextrapats:dredging), but copies the iota instead of moving it.

hextrogen:dash.d: Compels my mind to Dash according to the normalized vector. Cancels my velocity if given the zero vector. Free. If I am out of Dashes, does nothing. Requires Estrogen.

hextrogen:refresh_dashes.d: Instantly replenishes all of the player's Dashes. Costs about one [Charged Amethyst](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst). Nature *really* doesn't want me to dash infinitely, it seems. Requires Estrogen.

hexdim:dim/kidnap.d: You are going to ~~Brazil~~, ~~My Domain~~, *T H E   F U N   Z O N E*

hexdim:dim/kick.d: G E T   O U T

hexdim:dim/time.d: How much longer must I wait

hexxyskies:pos.d: Takes a position on a Ship and returns the associated Ship.

hexxyskies:zone_ship.d: Analogous to [Zone Distillation](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/entities@hexcasting:zone_entity), but instead returns a list of Ships.

hexxyskies:com/world.d: Analogous to [Compass Purification](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/basics@hexcasting:entity_pos/eye), but instead returns the position of a Ship's Center of Mass in [World Space](https://techtastic.github.io/HexxySkies/v/latest/master/en_us#basics/navimancy@hexxyskies:page/space/world).

hexxyskies:com/model.d: Analogous to [Compass Purification](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/basics@hexcasting:entity_pos/eye), but instead returns the position of a Ship's Center of Mass in [Model Space](https://techtastic.github.io/HexxySkies/v/latest/master/en_us#basics/navimancy@hexxyskies:page/space/model_body).

hexxyskies:mass.d: Takes either a Ship or a block location and returns the Ship's mass and the block's mass respectively.

hexxyskies:rot/euler.d: Returns the Ship's orientation as Euler Angles using the YXZ reference frame in radians.

hexxyskies:aabb.d:
Returns the minimum and maximum corners of the Ship's AABB in [Model Space](https://techtastic.github.io/HexxySkies/v/latest/master/en_us#basics/navimancy@hexxyskies:page/space/model_body).
Maybe using this with Hexstruction would allow you to disassemble the Ship...

hexxyskies:assemble.d: Takes in a list of positions to use to create a Ship. All positions must be in ambit. The cost is one shard per position. | Takes a mesh and creates a Ship from its points. All positions must be in ambit. The cost is one shard per position.

hexxyskies:scale/set.d: Scales the given Ship to the given size. The size must be between 1/16th and 16. Cost is one Shard times the size difference.

hexxyskies:force/world.d: Applies a [Force](https://techtastic.github.io/HexxySkies/v/latest/master/en_us#basics/navimancy@hexxyskies:page/forces_torques) at a given [World Space](https://techtastic.github.io/HexxySkies/v/latest/master/en_us#basics/navimancy@hexxyskies:page/space/world) position. The position is any offset from the [Center of Mass](https://techtastic.github.io/HexxySkies/v/latest/master/en_us#patterns/navimancy@hexxyskies:com/world) in World Space.

hexxyskies:torque/world.d: Applies a [Torque](https://techtastic.github.io/HexxySkies/v/latest/master/en_us#basics/navimancy@hexxyskies:page/forces_torques) specified by the vector in [World Space](https://techtastic.github.io/HexxySkies/v/latest/master/en_us#basics/navimancy@hexxyskies:page/space/world).

hexxyskies:force/model.d: Applies a [Force](https://techtastic.github.io/HexxySkies/v/latest/master/en_us#basics/navimancy@hexxyskies:page/forces_torques) at a given [Model Space](https://techtastic.github.io/HexxySkies/v/latest/master/en_us#basics/navimancy@hexxyskies:page/space/model_body) position. The position is any offset from the [Center of Mass](https://techtastic.github.io/HexxySkies/v/latest/master/en_us#patterns/navimancy@hexxyskies:com/model) in Model Space.

hexxyskies:torque/model.d: Applies a [Torque](https://techtastic.github.io/HexxySkies/v/latest/master/en_us#basics/navimancy@hexxyskies:page/forces_torques) specified by the vector in [Model Space](https://techtastic.github.io/HexxySkies/v/latest/master/en_us#basics/navimancy@hexxyskies:page/space/model_body)

hexxyskies:force/body.d: Applies a [Force](https://techtastic.github.io/HexxySkies/v/latest/master/en_us#basics/navimancy@hexxyskies:page/forces_torques) at a given [Body Space](https://techtastic.github.io/HexxySkies/v/latest/master/en_us#basics/navimancy@hexxyskies:page/space/model_body) position. The position is any offset from the Center of Mass in Body Space which is always (0, 0, 0).

hexxyskies:torque/body.d: Applies a [Torque](https://techtastic.github.io/HexxySkies/v/latest/master/en_us#basics/navimancy@hexxyskies:page/forces_torques)  specified by the vector in [Body Space](https://techtastic.github.io/HexxySkies/v/latest/master/en_us#basics/navimancy@hexxyskies:page/space/model_body).

hexxyskies:id.d: Returns the Ship's ID as a Long.

hexxyskies:rot/quaternion.d: Returns the Ship's orientation as a Quaternion.

hexxyskies:matrix/world_ship.d: Returns the Ship's World-to-Ship 4x4 transformation matrix.

hexxyskies:matrix/ship_world.d: Returns the Ship's Ship-to-World 4x4 transformation matrix.

hexxyskies:matrix/moment_of_inertia_tens.d: Returns the Ship's moment of inertia tensor as a 3x3 matrix.

hexxyplanes:get_plane.d: Retrieves an iota representing my hexplane.

hexxyplanes:plane_pos.d: Gets the spawn position within this plane as a vector.

hexxyplanes:plane_exit.d: Marks the target location as my exit for the hexplane, or resets it to be my spawn location if passed null, causing me to be sent there upon using [Planar Expulsion](https://real-septicake.github.io/HexxyPlanes/v/0.2.3+1.20.1/1.0/en_us#patterns/spells/hexplane@hexxyplanes:plane_banish) on myself.

hexxyplanes:exit_reveal.d: Displays my hexplane exit to me.

hexxyplanes:plane_banish.d: Forces the target out of the hexplane, costing 5 shards if used on something other than myself, and being free otherwise. Mishaps if not currently in a hexplane.

hexxyplanes:exit_deconstruct.d: Puts the dimension and the coordinates of my hexplane exit onto the stack.

hierophantics:villager_sleep.d: Causes the villager to seek out its bed and take a short nap. Not effective if the villager lacks a bed to use. Costs one [Charged Amethyst](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hierophantics:get_minds.d: Pushes a list of iotas representing all my embedded minds.

hierophantics:get_mind_hex.d: Pushes the Hex stored in the provided mind, or Null if there isn't one.

hierophantics:set_mind_hex.d: Stores the provided Hex into the mind. If there is already a stored Hex, it will be overwritten. Costs one [Charged Amethyst](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hierophantics:get_mind_trigger.d: Pushes the trigger stored in the provided mind, or Null if there isn't one.

hierophantics:set_mind_trigger.d: Stores the provided trigger into the mind. If the mind already has a trigger, it will be overwritten. Costs one [Amethyst Shard](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

hierophantics:mute_mind.d: Suppresses sound and particles from the provided mind's casting, based on the state of the bool. If true, the mind will be muted; if false, it will be unmuted.

hierophantics:free_mind.d:
Permanently removes an embedded mind from my own consciousness.
I wonder what happens to them when they go?

hierophantics:reenable_minds.d: When I die, my embedded minds become unstable and cease to function. This spell restores them to working order. Costs one [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst) per mind restored.

hierophantics:make_damage_trigger.d: Creates a trigger that activates whenever I take damage. To prevent a lethal chain-reaction, does not activate if the damage was caused by overcasting.

hierophantics:make_damage_type_trigger.d: Creates a trigger that activates whenever I take damage, but only if the damage was of a specific type. The trigger will be attuned to whatever type of damage I last received.

hierophantics:make_health_trigger.d: Creates a trigger that activates when my health drops below the specified value. A full, standard healthbar has a value of 20.

hierophantics:make_breath_trigger.d: Creates a trigger that activates when my breath drops below the specified value. A full bar of bubbles has a value of 10.

hierophantics:make_hunger_trigger.d: Creates a trigger that activates when my hunger drops below the specified value. A full hunger bar has a value of 20.

hierophantics:make_velocity_trigger.d: Creates a trigger that activates when my velocity (measured in blocks per tick) exceeds the specified value.

hierophantics:make_fall_trigger.d: Creates a trigger that activates when I fall further than the specified number of blocks.

hierophantics:make_drop_trigger.d: Creates a trigger that activates whenever I drop an item. This does **not** include involuntary dropping, such as on death or when using [Greater Teleport](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/great_spells/teleport).

hierophantics:make_attack_trigger.d: Creates a trigger that activates whenever I strike another entity.

hierophantics:make_break_trigger.d: Creates a trigger that activates whenever I break a block.

hierophantics:make_jump_trigger.d: Creates a trigger that activates whenever I jump.

hierophantics:make_teleport_trigger.d: Creates a trigger that activates whenever I teleport. For reasons I cannot discern, this will not detect teleports shorter than 1.5 blocks in length.

hierophantics:invert_trigger.d: Inverts the threshold on a numerical trigger. For example, 'When velocity exceeds 5.0' will become 'When velocity drops below 5.0'. Has no effect on other types of triggers.

hyperhexcast:range.d: Returns a list of nonnegative integers below the input. Mishaps if the input is less than 0.

hyperhexcast:getmt.d: Returns the entity that a given entity is riding. Null if the entity isn't riding anything.

hyperhexcast:getpsgr.d: Returns a list of entities that are riding a given entity.

hyperhexcast:isdrvr.d: Returns whether or not the given entity is considered the "Driver" of its vehicle. Null if the entity isn't riding a vehicle.

hyperhexcast:mount.d: Make an entity ride another entity. Costs about 2 [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst) if the top of the stack is a non-player entity, 1 if it is you, and about a crystal's worth if is it another player.

hyperhexcast:dismount.d: Make an entity stop riding the entity they are riding. Costs about 1 [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst), or a negligible amount when cast on yourself (but why would you).

ioticblocks:read/index.d:
Read a list iota out of an entity or block, then push the iota at the specified index to the stack.
It seems this and the next pattern may be useful for handling large amounts of data without causing a [Too Many Iotas](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#casting/mishaps) mishap.

ioticblocks:write/index.d: Read a list iota out of an entity or block, then set the element at the specified index of that list to the given iota, then write the resulting list back to the entity or block.

lapisworks:imbue_lap.d: Transform all the Lapis Lazuli in my other hand into Amethyst Lazuli, or Amel for short. Costs one Amethyst Shards in media and in item form (taken from my inventory) each, per Lapis.

lapisworks:reclaim_ameth.d: Transform all the Amethyst Lazuli in my other hand into twice as many Amethyst Shards. The Lapis turns into a fine mist which spreads quickly in the air. Excess shards spill onto the ground. Costs one shard.

lapisworks:swap_amel.d: Cycle through the appearances I've designed of the Amel or Amel-infused Construct (such as an Amel Ring) in my other hand. (e.g. Amel has four forms.)

lapisworks:moar_health.d: Pass in an entity and a number of half-hearts, and it enchants that entity's skin thus increasing their health. The Amel cost is the number given and the cost in media is twice the expended Amel.

lapisworks:moar_attack.d: Pass in an entity and a number of half-hearts, and it enchants their fists to increase their damage per hit. One Amel and five Amethyst Shards per half-heart. Limit is 4x the norm so just 4 for me.

lapisworks:moar_speed.d: Enchants the given entity's feet to increase their movement speed. Costs 1x Amel and 5x Amethyst Shards. Limit is 3x the norm. The norm for me is about 1.

lapisworks:gib_reach.d: Enchants the given *player's* arms (or disenchants if given false), increasing their reach by 3 blocks and their attack range by 1. Costs 16 Amel (or 0 if disenchanting) and four shards in media to change that player. There is no customizability here.

lapisworks:check_attr.d: Gives me the amount the given entity has been enhanced in the given area (specified by number). The patterns before were sorted such that 0 gives max health, 1 gives attack damage and so on. Negligible media cost.

lapisworks:fireyfists.d: Like Fire Aspect but for my hands. Costs 10 Charged Amethyst 48 Amel. Has one level. ID = 0.

lapisworks:lightningbending.d: 20 Charged Amethyst and a stack of Amel per level to bend the heavens to my will with my strikes. Three levels. ID = 1.

lapisworks:falldmgres.d: Cushions up to 20 blocks of fall damage per level, costing 5 Charged Amethyst and 20 Amel per level. Three levels. ID = 2.

lapisworks:longbreath.d: Enchant my lungs themselves to achieve the Respiration enchantment, but twice as strong. Two levels. 1 Charged Amethyst, 10 Amel. ID = 3.

lapisworks:fireresist.d: Wield the energy of an entire stack of Amel and 10 Charged Amethyst to make me hell-borne, essentially impervious to all heat. One level. ID = 4.

lapisworks:checkenchant.d: Gives the level of the specified (with ID) enchantment on the given entity for little cost and no Amel.

lapisworks:imbue_amel.d: The ancient "Lapisworkers" would use this often. Imbue the item in my hand with the specified amount of Amel, with no waste like the Enchant X spells. Costs 2x the amount of Amel being infused, in dust.

lapisworks:disimbue_amel.d: For one dust, tries to disimbue the item in my hand. If the item has multiple methods to make it then it the Amel has corroded it's original essence, resulting in disintegration into the least required Amel to make the item.

lapisworks:conjure_color.d: Conjures a fragile but solid block of the specified color at the provided position (which must be within range) for two amethyst dust. More explanation on the next page.

lapisworks:erase_color.d: Annihilates a block in range that would be cheap to break with [Break Block](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/spells/blockworks@hexcasting:break_block) for negligible cost, leaving no breaking or hex particles at all.

lapisworks:spherical_dstl.d: Evaluates (exactly like [Thoth's Gambit](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/meta@hexcasting:for_each)) the given pattern list over a hollow sphere with the given radius (non-decimal, at least 1, at most 64) around the given position.

lapisworks:spherical_dstl_filled.d: Like its Spherical Exaltation but for *filled* spheres.

lapisworks:cubic_exalt.d: Evaluates (exactly like [Thoth's Gambit](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/meta@hexcasting:for_each)) the given pattern list over a (hollow if given True) cube-ish area from the given points A to B.

lapisworks:empty_prfn.d: Answers the question, "is there only air there?" for negligible media cost. Vector must be in my ambit.

lapisworks:empty_dstl.d: Negligible cost. Answers the question, "are there no opaque blocks between these points?". Both vectors must be in my ambit.

lapisworks:visible_dstl.d: Negligible cost. Pushes whether or not the specified entity (within ambit) is able to see the specified block (also within ambit).

lapisworks:read_spechand.d: Specific hand version of [Scribe's Reflection](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/readwrite@hexcasting:read). Pushes the Iota stored in the Iota holder in the specified hand to the stack.

lapisworks:readable_spechand.d: Specific hand version of [Auditor's Reflection](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/readwrite@hexcasting:readable). Pushes whether the item in the specified hand can be read from or not.

lapisworks:write_spechand.d: Specific hand version of [Scribe's Gambit](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/readwrite@hexcasting:write). Writes the given Iota to the Iota holder in the specified hand.

lapisworks:writable_spechand.d: Specific hand version of [Assessor's Reflection](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/readwrite@hexcasting:writable). Pusher whether the item in the specified hand can be written to or not.

lapisworks:the_cooler_halt.d: [Charon's Gambit](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/meta@hexcasting:halt), if it could break through more than one layer. This pattern is useful in cases where [Charon's Gambit](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/meta@hexcasting:halt) is insufficient, however I wish not to delve into the complicated beast that is [Iris' Gambit](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/meta@hexcasting:eval/cc).

lapisworks:for_n_in_range.d:
*A oney and a twoey and a you-know-what-to-doey!*
Executes the given pattern list over a list of in(or de)crementing numbers, ranging from the first argument (inclusive) to the second (exclusive) as if [Thoth's Gambit](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/meta@hexcasting:for_each) were used.

lapisworks:execute_many_times.d:
*Do you know the definition of insanity?*
Executes the given pattern list the specified number of times. The stack on start behaves like it does for [Thoth's Gambit](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/meta@hexcasting:for_each).

lapisworks:hadamard.d: Based off the Hadamard Product, this pattern multiplies the respective elements of two vectors.

lapisworks:thewhattropy.d: Pops a list and pushes a random element of that list onto the stack.

lapisworks:min.d: Returns the smaller of the two numbers.

lapisworks:max.d: Returns the larger of the two numbers.

lapisworks:pull.d: Accelerates the given entity by the provided vector (like Impulse) for the specified amount of time (in twentieths of a second). Can be used to achieve drift/curve-shot-like effects. Costs the same as Impulse (including the subsequent cost per entity per cast) but multiplied by the time.

lapisworks:robbie_exalt.d:
Inserts the given iota into the given list before the specified index. An input of [a, b, c], 1, d would return [a, d, b, c].
*Arf, arf!*

lapisworks:get_datum.d: Pushes a list of the datum left to iterate over by the current Thoth's-like.

lapisworks:set_datum.d: Pops a list of iotas and sets the datum left to execute by the current Thoth's-like to that list.

lapisworks:get_thoth_hex.d: Pushes the instruction list the current Thoth's-like is executing.

lapisworks:set_thoth_hex.d: Pops a list of iotas and sets the instruction list of the current Thoth's-like to that list.

lapisworks:is_conjureable.d: Returns whether or not the block at the given coordinates within range is cheap to break with Break Block or not, for negligible cost.

lapisworks:thought_sieve.d: Sieves the torrent of information using the (full) artificial mind at the given position. 3/5 chance of replacing the pattern in my other hand with one of the correct stroke order.

lapisworks:absorb_mind.d: Absorbs the entirety of the mind within the container into the rechargeable item in my other hand. If there is any extra, it is discarded. A full container yields one Charged Amethyst.

lapisworks:check_mind.d: Pushes the percentage filled of the mind container at the given position to the stack.

lapisworks:teach_song.d: Teach the Live Jukebox at that location (which must be within ambit) these notes (a list of nums 0-24) at this frequency (0-20) for a shard of media. After being hit via Use, it plays the notes like an automatic Note Block.

lapisworks:song_purification.d: Divines from the specified Live Jukebox (within ambit) it's properties, and then returns a list of two elements. The first being the notes it plays, and the second being the frequency it plays them at. Free.

lapisworks:teach_simp.d: Teach the Simple Impetus at the provided coordinates (which must be within ambit) the provided pattern for two dust. The Simple Impetus will not remember this pattern when broken.

lapisworks:ask_simp.d: Simple Impeti are pretty gullible. Returns the pattern the Simple Impetus at the given location (which must be within ambit) is listening for, or null if it's not listening for any particular pattern. Free.

lapisworks:read_necklace.d: Reads the iota from the necklace I'm wearing. Mishaps if there is no readable one available. (Drawing aid: a line into almost a triangle, then a counterclockwise circle much like [Scribe's Reflection](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/readwrite@hexcasting:read).)

lapisworks:write_necklace.d: Writes the iota to the necklace I'm wearing. Mishaps if there is no writable one available. (Drawing aid: a line into almost a triangle, then a clockwise circle much like [Scribe's Gambit](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/readwrite@hexcasting:write).)

lapisworks:readable_necklace.d: Pushes if attempting to read from my necklace will succeed.

lapisworks:writeable_necklace.d: Pushes if attempting to write to my necklace will succeed.

lapisworks:deposit.d: Deposits as much of the specified amount (in dust) as possible. Costs the media deposited, plus a tax of 10% of it. Can never consume my health (or any "Bottomless Phials/Trinkets") for media.

lapisworks:withdraw.d: Withdraws, from the given Media Transfer Interface, into the Media-containing item in my other hand, as much of the dust specified as possible. Costs 10% of the media withdrawn.

lapisworks:get_mdia.d: Fetches the amount of media (in units of Amethyst Dust) contained in the given Media Transfer Interface.

lapisworks:phiangle.d: Phiangles two phiangleables. Costs a flat three Charged Amethyst, and a scalable one Amel per 32 blocks of distance, with a minimum of one.

lapisworks:dephiangle.d: Dephiangles two phiangleables, erasing the link between them. Costs three Charged Amethyst. I can cast this when I wish not to break the block, due to having other links for example.

lapisworks:get_linkable_links.d: Returns the positions the phiangleable at the specified position (within ambit) is phiangled to. Free.

lapisworks:get_amethyst_tuning.d: Returns the iota the Tuneable Amethyst at the specified position (within range) is tuned to.

lapisworks:tune_amethyst.d: Tunes the Tuneable Amethyst at the specified position (within range) to the specified iota. Costs a piece of Charged Amethyst and one Amel.

lapisworks:stop_be_me.d: The current One-time Ritual will no longer cast as it's starter.

lapisworks:be_me.d: The current One-time Ritual will cast as it's starter.

lapisworks:get_ritual_tuning.d: Fetches the frequency the current One-time Ritual is tuned to.

lapisworks:tune_ritual.d: Tunes the current One-time Ritual to the specified iota.

lapisworks:banish_my_enchsent.d: Peacefully put my Enchanted Sentinel to rest for a negligible amount of media, letting it rest for a time. Perhaps the ethical option, considering "falling apart" may not be the most painless.

lapisworks:banish_other_enchsent.d: Banish another's Enchanted Sentinel if it's at that block for 5 dust.

lapisworks:find_my_enchsent.d: Returns the location of my Enchanted Sentinel or null if I do not have one summoned.

lapisworks:gib_wisp_item.d: Swaps the item the provided wisp (that I must own) is holding and the provided item. Costs two and a half dust.

lapisworks:take_away_poor_baby_wisp_cand.d: Takes the item in the provided wisp (that I must own)'s offhand and lets it go into the world at the wisp's position. Costs two and a half dust.

lapisworks:get_amalgamation.d: Returns the Amalgamation in the container at the specified position (within range). Any changes to it are reflected in the block it came from.

lapisworks:get_amalgam_notiflevel.d: Returns the Amalgamation in the container at the specified position (within range). Any changes to it are reflected in the block it came from.

lapisworks:set_amalgam_notiflevel.d: Sets the provided amalgamation's loudness to the specified number (which must be positive and below 4).

lapisworks:get_amalgam_range.d: Pushes the range of the provided amalgamation.

lapisworks:set_amalgam_range.d: Sets the provided amalgamation's range to the specified number, mishapping if negative or out of bounds.

lapisworks:get_amalgam_greater.d: Pushes whether the provided amalgamation is Complex (true) or Simple (false).

lapisworks:get_self_amalgams_num.d: Pushes the number of amalgamations on my person.

lapisworks:remove_self_amalgam.d: Removes the amalgamation on my person with that index.

lapisworks:get_amalgam_err.d: Pushes the error of the provided amalgamation.

lapisworks:get_amalgam_hex.d: Pushes the hex that the amalgamation at the top of the stack would execute upon a successful trigger.

lapisworks:set_amalgam_hex.d: Sets the hex that the provided amalgamation would execute upon a successful trigger.

lessertp:lesser_tp.d: Pass in an entity within ambit and a vec, and the entity's fractional position will change to the vector (clamped). A number means a vec with all the components set to it. Negligible cost, but disappointing.

lessertp:simpler_tp.d: Takes an entity that will be within my ambit before and after teleportation and an offset vector, the length of which must be no greater than 16. Teleports the entity in that direction. Costs 2.5 dust.

moreiotas:string/empty.d: Add an empty string to the stack, useful for combining with other strings.

moreiotas:string/space.d: Add a blank space string to the stack, useful for combining with other strings.

moreiotas:string/comma.d: Add a comma string to the stack, useful for combining with other strings.

moreiotas:string/newline.d: Add a string to the stack representing a break between lines, useful for combining with other strings.

moreiotas:string/block/get.d: Removes a vector from the stack. If that vector is pointing at a sign or lectern, it returns that sign or lectern's text to the stack. Otherwise, it returns null.

moreiotas:string/block/set.d: Removes a vector and a string from the stack. If that vector is pointing at a sign or lectern, it writes that string to that sign or lectern. Costs a hundredth of an [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

moreiotas:string/chat/caster.d: Adds the last message the caster sent to the stack as a string.

moreiotas:string/chat/all.d: Adds the last message anyone sent to the stack as a string.

moreiotas:string/chat/prefix/get.d: Returns the last string you passed to [Sifter's Gambit](https://moreiotas.hexxy.media/v/0.1.2/1.0/en_us#patterns/strings@moreiotas:string/chat/prefix/set).

moreiotas:string/chat/prefix/set.d: Accepts a string; All future chat messages starting with that string won't be seen by others, and only messages prefixed with that string can be read by [Whisper Reflection](https://moreiotas.hexxy.media/v/0.1.2/1.0/en_us#patterns/strings@moreiotas:string/chat/caster).

moreiotas:string/iota.d: Converts the iota on top of the stack into a string.

moreiotas:string/action.d: Converts the pattern on top of the stack into the string for that pattern's name. If there is no action associated with that pattern, or if the associated pattern is a Great Spell, it returns null.

moreiotas:string/name/get.d: Takes an entity and returns that entity's name. If it is an item entity, return the item's name. | Takes a Ship and returns that Ship's slug.

moreiotas:string/name/set.d: Takes a string and an entity, and sets that entities name to the given string. If the entity is an item entity, also set the item's name. Costs a hundredth of an [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

moreiotas:string/split.d: Removes the top two strings from the stack and splits the first string, using the second string as the delimiter and returning as a list.

moreiotas:string/parse.d: Removes a string from the top of the stack and returns the number that string parses as (or null if it doesn't parse).

moreiotas:string/case.d: Removes a string and a bool or null. If it was true, return the string in upper case. If false, lowercase. If null, toggle each character's case.

moreiotas:altmul.d: Multiplies the first n by m matrix elementwise with another n by m matrix.

moreiotas:altdiv.d: Divides the first n by m matrix elementwise by another n by m matrix.

moreiotas:altpow.d: Raises the first n by m matrix elementwise to the power of another n by m matrix.

moreiotas:matrix/make.d: Converts the iota on top of the stack into a matrix. This iota can be a number, vector, or list.

moreiotas:matrix/unmake.d: Converts the iota on top of the stack back from a matrix into a number, vector, or list depending on the vector's size.

moreiotas:matrix/unmake/direct.d: As [Restoration Purification](https://moreiotas.hexxy.media/v/0.1.2/1.0/en_us#patterns/matrices@moreiotas:matrix/unmake), except it always returns a list of lists of numbers.

moreiotas:matrix/identity.d: Accepts a positive integer n, and returns an n by n matrix with 1 along the diagonal and 0 elsewhere.

moreiotas:matrix/zero.d: Accepts positive integers n and m, and returns an n by m matrix of zeros.

moreiotas:matrix/rotation.d: Accepts a vec v and number θ, and returns a matrix representing rotating by θ radians around v.

moreiotas:matrix/inverse.d: Accepts a matrix of any shappe and returns its inverse. For square matrices with a nonzero determinant, the inverse is the matrix such that in\*out = identity.

moreiotas:matrix/determinant.d: Accepts a square matrix and returns the determinant of that matrix.

moreiotas:matrix/concat/vert.d: Accepts an n by m matrix and a p by m matrix and produces a (n+p) by m matrix by putting the first matrix on top of the second.

moreiotas:matrix/concat/hori.d: Accepts an n by m matrix and an n by p matrix and produces an n by (m+p) matrix by putting the first matrix to the left of the second.

moreiotas:matrix/split/vert.d: Accepts an n by m matrix and an int from 0 to n, and returns two matrices created by splitting the input matrix vertically at the inputted int.

moreiotas:matrix/split/hori.d: Accepts an n by m matrix and an int from 0 to m, and returns two matrices created by splitting the input matrix horizontally at the inputted int.

moreiotas:type/to_item.d: Transforms the [Item Stack](https://moreiotas.hexxy.media/v/0.1.2/1.0/en_us#casting/item_iotas) at the top of the stack into its Item. | Accepts a mote and returns an [Item Stack](https://moreiotas.hexxy.media/v/0.1.2/1.0/en_us#casting/item_iotas) representing the items in the record referenced by that mote.

moreiotas:item/main_hand.d: Transforms the entity at the top of the stack into the Item Stack in its main hand. Also works on Item Frames and dropped items.

moreiotas:item/off_hand.d: Transforms the entity at the top of the stack into the Item Stack in its off hand.

moreiotas:item/inventory/stacks.d: Removes two vectors from the stack representing position and side. Returns a list of Item Stacks in the block at the given position accessible from the given side (or all if second vector is zero).

moreiotas:item/inventory/items.d: Removes two vectors from the stack representing position and side. Returns a list of Items in the block at the given position accessible from the given side (or all if second vector is zero).

moreiotas:item/make.d: Removes a number and either an itemtype or an Item Stack from the stack, then creates a new Item Stack with the specified item and size.

movesthemind:create.d: Bids the creature to the given location. Costs a charged amethyst.

movesthemind:destroy.d: Banishes the creature, making it disappear until I call it back. One Shard.

movesthemind:move/stopall.d: An important signal! Stops actions being performed by the creature, continuous and otherwise. Conveniently, an exception to the cost rule facing this page; It's free to cast.

movesthemind:move/look.d: Instructs the creature to look in a direction. The vector can be of any length. Seems to work on myself in the eyes of Nature, even though I don't feel or see the change.

movesthemind:move/walk.d: Instructs the creature to walk along its facing. A 1 beckons it forth, and a -1 backward. Interestingly, a 0 causes it to stop, as if I had halted it.

movesthemind:move/strafe.d: As previous, but along strafing. A 1, then, beckons it to the left, and a -1 to the right.

movesthemind:move/jump.d: Simply instructs the creature to hop. Also works on myself.

movesthemind:move/sneak.d: Takes a boolean and tells the creature to start or stop sneaking. Also seems to work on myself, until my synapses kick in a moment after. Maybe it could be of use with other bids?

movesthemind:move/sprint.d: As previous, but with sprinting. Even when stationary, the creature produces sprinting particles to denote its intention.

movesthemind:move/use.d:
Now, an interesting pair of instructions. Begin to use or attack with the held item at an interval, in twentieths of a second. 
Both work on myself, though the former strangely.

movesthemind:move/attack.d: Given 0, uses it continuously, such as eating or channeling, or in the case of Attack, mining. Given -1, uses or attacks once and stops.

movesthemind:move/hotbar.d: Takes a number from 1 to 9 inclusive, and instructs to select that slot in its toolbar. Works on myself, but may interrupt things like drawing patterns.

movesthemind:move/swap_hands.d: Instructs the creature to hand its mainhand item into its offhand, and vice versa. As previous, in its function to myself.

movesthemind:move/drop.d: Instructs the creature to drop the item or stack of items it holds in its main hand. Can even yank an item from my own hand, as I'm so familiar with.

oneironaut:getdim1.d: Returns a Spatial Imprint representing the dimension I am currently in. Costs a negligible amount of media.

oneironaut:getdim2.d: Returns a Spatial Imprint representing the dimension my sentinel is currently in. Costs one-tenth of an amethyst dust.

oneironaut:getdim/overworld.d: Returns a Spatial Imprint representing the overworld. Costs one-tenth of an amethyst dust.

oneironaut:getdim/nether.d:
Returns a Spatial Imprint representing the nether. Costs one-tenth of an amethyst dust.
There seems to be some resistance when I cast this. Perhaps I'll be able to overcome it with greater skill...

oneironaut:getdimheight.d: Accepts a Spatial Imprint, and returns the lowest and highest altitudes at which blocks can exist in the corresponding dimension.

oneironaut:getdimscale.d: Accepts a Spatial Imprint, and returns how many blocks you'd have to travel in the overworld to travel the equivalent of one block in the input dimension.

oneironaut:getrodlook.d: When cast with a Reverberation Rod, returns my look vector from when I started the current cast loop.

oneironaut:getrodpos.d: When cast with a Reverberation Rod, returns my eye position from when I started the current cast loop.

oneironaut:getrodstamp.d: When cast with a Reverberation Rod, returns the timestamp from when I started the current cast loop.

oneironaut:readrodram.d: Returns the iota stored in the current cast loop. Defaults to NULL.

oneironaut:writerodram.d: Accepts a non-list iota, and stores it inside the current cast loop. It will be lost when the cast loop ends.

oneironaut:readrodramremote.d: As Williams' Reflection, but can be cast from non-rod sources while a rod is in use.

oneironaut:writerodramremote.d: As Williams' Gambit, but can be cast from non-rod sources while a rod is in use.

oneironaut:readidea.d: Accepts a valid key, and returns the corresponding iota. Costs one-eigth of an amethyst dust.

oneironaut:readideatime.d: Accepts a valid key, and returns when the corresponding iota was inscribed, or -1. Costs no media.

oneironaut:readideawriter.d: Accepts a valid key and a player, and returns whether the corresponding iota was inscribed by that player. Costs no media.

oneironaut:readsentinel.d: Accepts a vector and a player, and returns either the distance from the vector to the target player's sentinel or NULL. Costs a negligible amount of media.

oneironaut:detectshroud.d: Accepts a vector and a number, and returns a list of unit vectors pointing from the initial vector to shrouded entities within a radius defined by the number.

oneironaut:delayrod.d: Accepts a positive integer. When cast with a Reverberation Rod, delays the current cast loop's next cast until that many twentieths of a second have passed.

oneironaut:haltrod.d: When cast with a Reverberation Rod, forcibly halts the current cast loop.

oneironaut:resetrod.d: Accepts a positive integer. Halts the current cast loop but also reduces the cooldown period from 1 second to ((1/20) \* number) seconds. Cooldown due to mishap is unaffected.

oneironaut:queryrod.d: Returns a boolean corresponding to whether the current cast is making use of a rod.

oneironaut:rodloopactive.d: Returns whether the caster is currently using a rod, regardless of the current cast is from that rod.

oneironaut:writeidea.d: Accepts a valid key and any iota, and stores it in the corresponding location. Costs a quarter of an amethyst dust.

oneironaut:craftrod.d: Acts just like [the spells used to program conventional casting items](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/spells/hexcasting). Costs 10 Charged Amethyst.

oneironaut:craftbottomlesstrinket.d: Writes a hex to the bottomless trinket in my other hand. Costs ten charged amethyst.

oneironaut:shiftsentinel.d: Accepts a spatial imprint, and moves my sentinel to its scaled coordinates in the corresponding dimension. Costs one amethyst shard. Mishaps if I do not currently have a sentinel.

overevaluate:swap_one_three.d: Reflects the order of the top three iota, turning A, B, C into C, B, A. Essentially swaps the top and the third-from-the-top iota.

overevaluate:swap_two_three.d: Causes the third-from-the-top iota to bubble up over the second-from-the-top iota, essentially swapping them.

overevaluate:dup_many.d: Takes a number and duplicates that many elements of the stack while preserving order.

overevaluate:create_jumble.d: Creates a jumble iota corresponding to the argument count and the list of numbers.

overevaluate:dissolve_jumble.d: Dissolves a jumble iota back into a number and a list of numbers.

overevaluate:soroban_increment.d: Pushes soroban's current value and then increases it. Starts at 0.

overevaluate:soroban_set.d: Pops a number from the stack and sets the soroban to it.

overevaluate:apep.d: Folds across the first list using the Hex in the second list.

overevaluate:athena.d: Casts a list of patterns similar to [Hermes' Gambit](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/meta@hexcasting:eval) but allows for handling of mishaps.

overevaluate:athena_print.d: Reveals to me the last mishap caught by [Athena's Gambit](https://miyucomics.github.io/overevaluate/v/latest/main/en_us#metaevals@overevaluate:athena) within this Hex.

overevaluate:athena_log.d: Pushes the last mishap caught by [Athena's Gambit](https://miyucomics.github.io/overevaluate/v/latest/main/en_us#metaevals@overevaluate:athena) as *text* if the appropriate powers are active in this world.

overevaluate:atalanta.d: Should only be run inside [Thoth's](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/meta@hexcasting:for_each) or [Sisyphus' Gambit](https://miyucomics.github.io/overevaluate/v/latest/main/en_us#metaevals@overevaluate:sisyphus). Acts similarly to [Charon's Gambit](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/meta@hexcasting:halt) except does not end the iterator, only skips the rest of the current iteration.

overevaluate:castor.d: Should only be run within a [Thoth's](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/meta@hexcasting:for_each). Details on the next page. Beware of triggering the Delve Too Deep mishap.

overevaluate:pollux.d: Sibling pattern to [Castor's Gambit](https://miyucomics.github.io/overevaluate/v/latest/main/en_us#metaevals@overevaluate:castor), this pattern schedules the additional iteration for the end instead. Carries the same risk of encountering the Delve Too Deep mishap.

overevaluate:janus.d: Instantly terminates the Hex regardless of current circumstances.

overevaluate:maat.d: Takes a boolean and any iota. If the boolean is false, mishaps and prints the iota.

overevaluate:sisyphus.d: Takes a pattern list and casts it over and over forever until it encounters either a [Charon's Gambit](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/meta@hexcasting:halt) or a [Janus' Gambit](https://miyucomics.github.io/overevaluate/v/latest/main/en_us#metaevals@overevaluate:janus).

overevaluate:themis.d: Takes a list and a pattern or pattern list which is used to sort the list by casting over every iota similar to [Thoth's Gambit](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/meta@hexcasting:for_each).

scryglass:get_window_size.d: Returns the full width and height of my vision as a vector.

scryglass:get_icons.d: Pushes a list of the indices of all the Icons I have. This appears as a list of numbers.

scryglass:draw_text.d: Takes an index, a position, a number, and any iota. Conjures an Icon displaying that iota.

scryglass:draw_rect.d: Takes an index, a position, a size, and a color. Conjures an Icon displaying that rectangle.

scryglass:draw_line.d: Takes an index, a position, a size, and a color. Conjures an Icon that joins between the two with a thin line.

scryglass:rotate_icon.d: Takes an index and an amount of rotation counterclockwise in terms of a full circle. Rotates the icon.

scryglass:scale_icon.d: Takes an index and a scaling factor. Scales the icon.

slate_work:store_item.d: It is much easier to store an item into a Vessel than to pull it out. This pattern simply takes an Item Entity, and neatly sorts it into the activated Storage Vessels. Costs an 1/8th of a [dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst) per activated Vessel.

slate_work:get_storage.d: This simply returns what Vessels the current [Spell Circle](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#greatwork/spellcircles) has activated. I should likely use this to check if the [Spell Circle](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#greatwork/spellcircles) has collected any Vessels.

slate_work:get_item.d: This takes a Hex and runs it on every [Item Stack](https://moreiotas.hexxy.media/v/0.1.2/1.0/en_us#patterns/items) stored (with it on top of the stack). Once the Hex is executed, it requires a Integer, Vector, and Boolean, left on the stack, in that order.

slate_work:check_item.d: Check Item functions much like Reawaken Item; however, it only requires a Boolean from the inputted Hex. If the Boolean is ever True, the spell ends, and returns True.

slate_work:sort_items.d: In some rare scenarios, Vessels can get jumbled up and have items of the same type spread across different  Vessels. This is a neat spell to resort them at a cost. That cost being 5 [Charged Amethyst](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

slate_work:set_craft.d: Sets the crafting recipe of a [Patterned Assembler](https://stick404.github.io/SlateWork/v/2.2.0/1.0/en_us#greatwork/crafting_loci). Takes a list of [Nulls](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#casting/101), items, or item variants, and applies it to the targeted [Assembler](https://stick404.github.io/SlateWork/v/2.2.0/1.0/en_us#greatwork/crafting_loci).

slate_work:get_craft_count.d: This gets how many times the [Patterned Assembler](https://stick404.github.io/SlateWork/v/2.2.0/1.0/en_us#greatwork/crafting_loci) will craft a recipe.

slate_work:set_craft_count.d: This sets how many times the [Patterned Assembler](https://stick404.github.io/SlateWork/v/2.2.0/1.0/en_us#greatwork/crafting_loci) will craft a recipe.

slate_work:set_macro.d:
This binds both a pattern and an iota to a [Spell Imprinter](https://stick404.github.io/SlateWork/v/2.2.0/1.0/en_us#greatwork/macro_loci), which is at the targeted vector. 
Does not mishap if casted outside of a [Spell Circle](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#greatwork/spellcircles). Costs a negligible amount of media.

slate_work:set_sents.d: This takes a list of vectors, and attempts to move the Pseudosentinels to the positions.

slate_work:get_sents.d: This retrieves the current positions of all Pseudosentinels in the order they were awoken. Free to cast.

slate_work:read_broadcast.d:
Attempts to read an [Iotic Door](https://stick404.github.io/SlateWork/v/2.2.0/1.0/en_us#greatwork/broadcaster_loci) at the given vector. If there is not a [Door](https://stick404.github.io/SlateWork/v/2.2.0/1.0/en_us#greatwork/broadcaster_loci), returns garbage. 
Does not mishap if casted outside of a [Spell Circle](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#greatwork/spellcircles), free, and does not require ambit.

slate_work:set_slot.d: This takes a number between 0 and 5 (inclusive), and sets the held slot of the bound [Pocket Simulator](https://stick404.github.io/SlateWork/v/2.2.0/1.0/en_us#greatwork/hotbar_loci). Free.

slate_work:get_items.d: This returns all the items held within the [Pocket Simulator](https://stick404.github.io/SlateWork/v/2.2.0/1.0/en_us#greatwork/hotbar_loci) as [Item Stack Iotas](https://moreiotas.hexxy.media/v/0.1.2/1.0/en_us#patterns/items). Free.

slate_work:get_trades.d: Despite the return of this spell, its not extremely complicated... I think. This takes a [Merchant Directrix](https://stick404.github.io/SlateWork/v/2.2.0/1.0/en_us#greatwork/trade_loci), and returns: [[Item Stack, Item Stack, Item Stack, Number]...]. Free to cast.

slate_work:exchange_mind.d: This feels... [familiar](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#patterns/great_spells/brainsweep). This spell takes a Villager, and a [Merchant Directrix](https://stick404.github.io/SlateWork/v/2.2.0/1.0/en_us#greatwork/trade_loci) and exchanges their Jobs. Costs 1 [Charged Amethyst](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst) to reapply the knowledge of Working.

slate_work:wave_position.d: Adds the current position of the Media Wave to the top of the stack.

slate_work:wave_normal.d: Adds the current facing of the Media Wave to the top of the stack. If the current block does not have a facing, it returns a vector of [0,0,0].

slate_work:wave_speed.d: Adds the current speed of the Media Wave to the top of the stack. This is measured in how many 20ths of a second the Media Wave waits until going to the next [Slate.](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/slate)

slate_work:media_reflection.d: Adds the current amount of Media in the Impetus to the stack, in units of [dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

efhexs:set_target.d: Sets a list of players to be exclusively influenced by my special effects. If [Null](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#casting/101), all can see my effects again.

efhexs:get_sounds.d: Pushes the last sixteen unique sounds that I have heard.

efhexs:play_sound.d: Plays a sound at a particular location, volume, and pitch. Costs about a sixteenth of an [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

efhexs:get_particles.d: Pushes the last sixteen unique particles that have happened around me.

efhexs:play_particle.d: Conjures a particular particle with a specified position and velocity (blocks per twentieth of a second). Costs about 1/32th of an [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

efhexs:play_dust_particle.d: Conjures a small mote of dust of a given color. The number relates vaguely to scale and lifespan.

efhexs:play_dust_transition_particle.d: Conjures a gradient-like mote of dust, which smoothly transitions between the two colors given over the given number of seconds.

efhexs:play_block_particle.d: Conjures a visual bit of debris, similar to that caused by breaking a block. Takes in a block identifier.

efhexs:play_falling_dust_particle.d: Conjures particles similar to that caused by suspended gravity-affected blocks. Takes in a block identifier.

efhexs:play_item_particle.d: Conjures a visual bit of fragments, similar to that caused by a tool breaking after wearing. Takes in an item iota.

efhexs:play_hex_particle.d: Conjures a blob of visible media, not unlike the waste product of my Hexes. Takes in a color.

efhexs:play_potion_effect.d: Conjures a swirling particle like the ones that emanate from me when I am under the effects of a potion. Takes in a color.

efhexs:play_item_pickup.d: Conjures an illusion of the given item iota at the location and makes it fly into the given entity before disappearing, as though the entity had picked it up.

yaha:paper_plane.d: Summons a projectile that slowly flies towards the given entity, dealing 3 hearts of damage. Costs one [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst). Adds itself onto the stack.

yaha:paper_plane_target.d: Returns the target of a paper plane, or null if it does not have one.

yaha:time_bomb.d: Summons a floating projectile that casts after a given duration. Costs one [Charged Amethyst](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst), plus the media given to the bomb. Adds itself onto the stack.

yaha:time_bomb_pos.d: Returns the position of the time bomb casting this pattern. Mishaps if not cast by a bomb.

yaha:anvil.d: Summons an anvil that deals damage based on its velocity. Damage dealt never goes above 10 hearts. Costs one [Charged Amethyst](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst). Adds itself onto the stack.

yaha:trident.d: Summons a trident that pierces mobs and pulls them inwards. Costs one [Charged Amethyst](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst). Adds itself onto the stack.

yaha:sussify_block.d: Buries the item entity into a sand or gravel block, forming suspicious sand/gravel. Costs an eighth of an [Amethyst Dust](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

yaha:potion_to_item.d: Plucks a potion out of the air, turning it into an item entity. Costs one [Charged Amethyst](https://hexcasting.hexxy.media/v/0.11.4/1.0/en_us#items/amethyst).

yaha:stand_toggle_arms.d: Gives the armor stand arms. Casting again removes the armor stand's arms.

yaha:stand_toggle_base.d: Vanishes the stone baseplate supporting the armor stand. Casting again rematerializes the baseplate.

yaha:stand_toggle_tiny.d: Gives the armor stand a smaller form. Casting again brings it back to its original size.

yaha:stand_rotate_head.d: The pattern with the left protrusion orients the armor stand's head; the pattern with the right protrusion orients the armor stand's torso.

yaha:stand_rotate_body.d: The pattern with the left protrusion orients the armor stand's head; the pattern with the right protrusion orients the armor stand's torso.

yaha:stand_rotate_yaw.d: Faces the armor stand towards the given yaw in radians, where south is 0 rad, west is π/2 rad, north is π rad, and east is -π/2 rad.

yaha:stand_rotate_left_arm.d: The pattern with the left protrusion orients the armor stand's left arm; the pattern with the right protrusion orients the armor stand's right arm.

yaha:stand_rotate_right_arm.d: The pattern with the left protrusion orients the armor stand's left arm; the pattern with the right protrusion orients the armor stand's right arm.

yaha:stand_rotate_left_leg.d: The pattern with the left protrusion orients the armor stand's left leg; the pattern with the right protrusion orients the armor stand's right leg.

yaha:stand_rotate_right_leg.d: The pattern with the left protrusion orients the armor stand's left leg; the pattern with the right protrusion orients the armor stand's right leg.

mediatransport:send_fsb.d: Sends the iota on the top of the stack into the ether to be received by my current avatar. Can fail for [various reasons](https://penguinencounter.github.io/mediatransport/v/1.1.1+1.20.1/2.0/en_us#interop/figura/mishaps). Always costs a fixed 1 'sending power.'

mediatransport:recv_fsb.d: Retrieves the next iota from the inbound queue, or [mishaps](https://penguinencounter.github.io/mediatransport/v/1.1.1+1.20.1/2.0/en_us#interop/figura/mishaps) if the queue is empty.

mediatransport:check_queue.d: Queries the number of iotas in the queue.

mediatransport:check_rate_limit.d: Queries the amount of 'sending power' remaining.

mediatransport:send_server_info.d: Asks Nature to send information about its preferences to my current avatar. Costs 1 'spending power'. See [the protocol documentation](https://penguinencounter.github.io/mediatransport/v/1.1.1+1.20.1/2.0/en_us#mediatransport_virtual/protocol) for details.

hexthings:unquote.d: This pattern can be used to place raw iota directly into an Introspection-Restrospection pair. After drawing this pattern, all subsequent patterns are "unescaped", allowing them to be executed as normal until a [Retrojection](https://real-septicake.github.io/HexThings/v/0.1.8+1.20.1/1.2/en_us#patterns/hexutils@hexthings:requote) is encountered.
